1:1.web: There was a man in the land of Uz, whose name was Job. That man was blameless and upright, and one who feared God, and turned away from evil.
1:1.kjv: There was a man in the land of Uz, whose name was Job; and that man was perfect and upright, and one that feared God, and eschewed evil.

1:2.web: There were born to him seven sons and three daughters.
1:2.kjv: And there were born unto him seven sons and three daughters.

1:3.web: His possessions also were seven thousand sheep, three thousand camels, five hundred yoke of oxen, five hundred female donkeys, and a very great household; so that this man was the greatest of all the children of the east.
1:3.kjv: His substance also was seven thousand sheep, and three thousand camels, and five hundred yoke of oxen, and five hundred she asses, and a very great household; so that this man was the greatest of all the men of the east.

1:4.web: His sons went and held a feast in the house of each one on his birthday; and they sent and called for their three sisters to eat and to drink with them.
1:4.kjv: And his sons went and feasted in their houses, every one his day; and sent and called for their three sisters to eat and to drink with them.

1:5.web: It was so, when the days of their feasting had run their course, that Job sent and sanctified them, and rose up early in the morning, and offered burnt offerings according to the number of them all. For Job said, “It may be that my sons have sinned, and renounced God in their hearts.” Job did so continually.
1:5.kjv: And it was so, when the days of their feasting were gone about, that Job sent and sanctified them, and rose up early in the morning, and offered burnt offerings according to the number of them all: for Job said, It may be that my sons have sinned, and cursed God in their hearts. Thus did Job continually.

1:6.web: Now on the day when God’s sons came to present themselves before Yahweh, Satan also came among them.
1:6.kjv: Now there was a day when the sons of God came to present themselves before the LORD, and Satan came also among them.

1:7.web: Yahweh said to Satan, “Where have you come from?” Then Satan answered Yahweh, and said, “From going back and forth in the earth, and from walking up and down in it.”
1:7.kjv: And the LORD said unto Satan, Whence comest thou? Then Satan answered the LORD, and said, From going to and fro in the earth, and from walking up and down in it.

1:8.web: Yahweh said to Satan, “Have you considered my servant, Job? For there is no one like him in the earth, a blameless and an upright man, one who fears God, and turns away from evil.”
1:8.kjv: And the LORD said unto Satan, Hast thou considered my servant Job, that there is none like him in the earth, a perfect and an upright man, one that feareth God, and escheweth evil?

1:9.web: Then Satan answered Yahweh, and said, “Does Job fear God for nothing?
1:9.kjv: Then Satan answered the LORD, and said, Doth Job fear God for nought?

1:10.web: Haven’t you made a hedge around him, and around his house, and around all that he has, on every side? You have blessed the work of his hands, and his substance is increased in the land.
1:10.kjv: Hast not thou made an hedge about him, and about his house, and about all that he hath on every side? thou hast blessed the work of his hands, and his substance is increased in the land.

1:11.web: But stretch out your hand now, and touch all that he has, and he will renounce you to your face.”
1:11.kjv: But put forth thine hand now, and touch all that he hath, and he will curse thee to thy face.

1:12.web: Yahweh said to Satan, “Behold, all that he has is in your power. Only on himself don’t stretch out your hand.” So Satan went out from the presence of Yahweh.
1:12.kjv: And the LORD said unto Satan, Behold, all that he hath is in thy power; only upon himself put not forth thine hand. So Satan went forth from the presence of the LORD.

1:13.web: It fell on a day when his sons and his daughters were eating and drinking wine in their oldest brother’s house,
1:13.kjv: And there was a day when his sons and his daughters were eating and drinking wine in their eldest brother’s house:

1:14.web: that there came a messenger to Job, and said, “The oxen were plowing, and the donkeys feeding beside them,
1:14.kjv: And there came a messenger unto Job, and said, The oxen were plowing, and the asses feeding beside them:

1:15.web: and the Sabeans attacked, and took them away. Yes, they have killed the servants with the edge of the sword, and I alone have escaped to tell you.”
1:15.kjv: And the Sabeans fell upon them, and took them away; yea, they have slain the servants with the edge of the sword; and I only am escaped alone to tell thee.

1:16.web: While he was still speaking, there also came another, and said, “The fire of God has fallen from the sky, and has burned up the sheep and the servants, and consumed them, and I alone have escaped to tell you.”
1:16.kjv: While he was yet speaking, there came also another, and said, The fire of God is fallen from heaven, and hath burned up the sheep, and the servants, and consumed them; and I only am escaped alone to tell thee.

1:17.web: While he was still speaking, there came also another, and said, “The Chaldeans made three bands, and swept down on the camels, and have taken them away, yes, and killed the servants with the edge of the sword; and I alone have escaped to tell you.”
1:17.kjv: While he was yet speaking, there came also another, and said, The Chaldeans made out three bands, and fell upon the camels, and have carried them away, yea, and slain the servants with the edge of the sword; and I only am escaped alone to tell thee.

1:18.web: While he was still speaking, there came also another, and said, “Your sons and your daughters were eating and drinking wine in their oldest brother’s house,
1:18.kjv: While he was yet speaking, there came also another, and said, Thy sons and thy daughters were eating and drinking wine in their eldest brother’s house:

1:19.web: and behold, there came a great wind from the wilderness, and struck the four corners of the house, and it fell on the young men, and they are dead. I alone have escaped to tell you.”
1:19.kjv: And, behold, there came a great wind from the wilderness, and smote the four corners of the house, and it fell upon the young men, and they are dead; and I only am escaped alone to tell thee.

1:20.web: Then Job arose, and tore his robe, and shaved his head, and fell down on the ground, and worshiped.
1:20.kjv: Then Job arose, and rent his mantle, and shaved his head, and fell down upon the ground, and worshipped,

1:21.web: He said, “Naked I came out of my mother’s womb, and naked shall I return there. Yahweh gave, and Yahweh has taken away. Blessed be Yahweh’s name.”
1:21.kjv: And said, Naked came I out of my mother’s womb, and naked shall I return thither: the LORD gave, and the LORD hath taken away; blessed be the name of the LORD.

1:22.web: In all this, Job did not sin, nor charge God with wrongdoing.
1:22.kjv: In all this Job sinned not, nor charged God foolishly.

2:1.web: Again, on the day when the God’s sons came to present themselves before Yahweh, Satan came also among them to present himself before Yahweh.
2:1.kjv: Again there was a day when the sons of God came to present themselves before the LORD, and Satan came also among them to present himself before the LORD.

2:2.web: Yahweh said to Satan, “Where have you come from?” Satan answered Yahweh, and said, “From going back and forth in the earth, and from walking up and down in it.”
2:2.kjv: And the LORD said unto Satan, From whence comest thou? And Satan answered the LORD, and said, From going to and fro in the earth, and from walking up and down in it.

2:3.web: Yahweh said to Satan, “Have you considered my servant Job? For there is no one like him in the earth, a blameless and an upright man, one who fears God, and turns away from evil. He still maintains his integrity, although you incited me against him, to ruin him without cause.”
2:3.kjv: And the LORD said unto Satan, Hast thou considered my servant Job, that there is none like him in the earth, a perfect and an upright man, one that feareth God, and escheweth evil? and still he holdeth fast his integrity, although thou movedst me against him, to destroy him without cause.

2:4.web: Satan answered Yahweh, and said, “Skin for skin. Yes, all that a man has he will give for his life.
2:4.kjv: And Satan answered the LORD, and said, Skin for skin, yea, all that a man hath will he give for his life.

2:5.web: But stretch out your hand now, and touch his bone and his flesh, and he will renounce you to your face.”
2:5.kjv: But put forth thine hand now, and touch his bone and his flesh, and he will curse thee to thy face.

2:6.web: Yahweh said to Satan, “Behold, he is in your hand. Only spare his life.”
2:6.kjv: And the LORD said unto Satan, Behold, he is in thine hand; but save his life.

2:7.web: So Satan went out from the presence of Yahweh, and struck Job with painful sores from the sole of his foot to his head.
2:7.kjv: So went Satan forth from the presence of the LORD, and smote Job with sore boils from the sole of his foot unto his crown.

2:8.web: He took for himself a potsherd to scrape himself with, and he sat among the ashes.
2:8.kjv: And he took him a potsherd to scrape himself withal; and he sat down among the ashes.

2:9.web: Then his wife said to him, “Do you still maintain your integrity? Renounce God, and die.”
2:9.kjv: Then said his wife unto him, Dost thou still retain thine integrity? curse God, and die.

2:10.web: But he said to her, “You speak as one of the foolish women would speak. What? Shall we receive good at the hand of God, and shall we not receive evil?” In all this Job didn’t sin with his lips.
2:10.kjv: But he said unto her, Thou speakest as one of the foolish women speaketh. What? shall we receive good at the hand of God, and shall we not receive evil? In all this did not Job sin with his lips.

2:11.web: Now when Job’s three friends heard of all this evil that had come on him, they each came from his own place: Eliphaz the Temanite, Bildad the Shuhite, and Zophar the Naamathite; and they made an appointment together to come to sympathize with him and to comfort him.
2:11.kjv: Now when Job’s three friends heard of all this evil that was come upon him, they came every one from his own place; Eliphaz the Temanite, and Bildad the Shuhite, and Zophar the Naamathite: for they had made an appointment together to come to mourn with him and to comfort him.

2:12.web: When they lifted up their eyes from a distance, and didn’t recognize him, they raised their voices, and wept; and they each tore his robe, and sprinkled dust on their heads toward the sky.
2:12.kjv: And when they lifted up their eyes afar off, and knew him not, they lifted up their voice, and wept; and they rent every one his mantle, and sprinkled dust upon their heads toward heaven.

2:13.web: So they sat down with him on the ground seven days and seven nights, and no one spoke a word to him, for they saw that his grief was very great.
2:13.kjv: So they sat down with him upon the ground seven days and seven nights, and none spake a word unto him: for they saw that his grief was very great.

3:1.web: After this Job opened his mouth, and cursed the day of his birth.
3:1.kjv: After this opened Job his mouth, and cursed his day.

3:3.web: “Let the day perish in which I was born, the night which said, ‘There is a boy conceived.’
3:3.kjv: Let the day perish wherein I was born, and the night in which it was said, There is a man child conceived.

3:4.web: Let that day be darkness. Don’t let God from above seek for it, neither let the light shine on it.
3:4.kjv: Let that day be darkness; let not God regard it from above, neither let the light shine upon it.

3:5.web: Let darkness and the shadow of death claim it for their own. Let a cloud dwell on it. Let all that makes black the day terrify it.
3:5.kjv: Let darkness and the shadow of death stain it; let a cloud dwell upon it; let the blackness of the day terrify it.

3:6.web: As for that night, let thick darkness seize on it. Let it not rejoice among the days of the year. Let it not come into the number of the months.
3:6.kjv: As for that night, let darkness seize upon it; let it not be joined unto the days of the year, let it not come into the number of the months.

3:7.web: Behold, let that night be barren. Let no joyful voice come therein.
3:7.kjv: Lo, let that night be solitary, let no joyful voice come therein.

3:8.web: Let them curse it who curse the day, who are ready to rouse up leviathan.
3:8.kjv: Let them curse it that curse the day, who are ready to raise up their mourning.

3:9.web: Let the stars of its twilight be dark. Let it look for light, but have none, neither let it see the eyelids of the morning,
3:9.kjv: Let the stars of the twilight thereof be dark; let it look for light, but have none; neither let it see the dawning of the day:

3:10.web: because it didn’t shut up the doors of my mother’s womb, nor did it hide trouble from my eyes.
3:10.kjv: Because it shut not up the doors of my mother’s womb, nor hid sorrow from mine eyes.

3:11.web: “Why didn’t I die from the womb? Why didn’t I give up the spirit when my mother bore me?
3:11.kjv: Why died I not from the womb? why did I not give up the ghost when I came out of the belly?

3:12.web: Why did the knees receive me? Or why the breast, that I should nurse?
3:12.kjv: Why did the knees prevent me? or why the breasts that I should suck?

3:13.web: For now should I have lain down and been quiet. I should have slept, then I would have been at rest,
3:13.kjv: For now should I have lain still and been quiet, I should have slept: then had I been at rest,

3:14.web: with kings and counselors of the earth, who built up waste places for themselves;
3:14.kjv: With kings and counsellors of the earth, which built desolate places for themselves;

3:15.web: or with princes who had gold, who filled their houses with silver:
3:15.kjv: Or with princes that had gold, who filled their houses with silver:

3:16.web: or as a hidden untimely birth I had not been, as infants who never saw light.
3:16.kjv: Or as an hidden untimely birth I had not been; as infants which never saw light.

3:17.web: There the wicked cease from troubling. There the weary are at rest.
3:17.kjv: There the wicked cease from troubling; and there the weary be at rest.

3:18.web: There the prisoners are at ease together. They don’t hear the voice of the taskmaster.
3:18.kjv: There the prisoners rest together; they hear not the voice of the oppressor.

3:19.web: The small and the great are there. The servant is free from his master.
3:19.kjv: The small and great are there; and the servant is free from his master.

3:20.web: “Why is light given to him who is in misery, life to the bitter in soul,
3:20.kjv: Wherefore is light given to him that is in misery, and life unto the bitter in soul;

3:21.web: Who long for death, but it doesn’t come; and dig for it more than for hidden treasures,
3:21.kjv: Which long for death, but it cometh not; and dig for it more than for hid treasures;

3:22.web: who rejoice exceedingly, and are glad, when they can find the grave?
3:22.kjv: Which rejoice exceedingly, and are glad, when they can find the grave?

bsb: Why is life given to a man
3:23.web: Why is light given to a man whose way is hidden, whom God has hedged in?
3:23.kjv: Why is light given to a man whose way is hid, and whom God hath hedged in?

3:24.web: For my sighing comes before I eat. My groanings are poured out like water.
3:24.kjv: For my sighing cometh before I eat, and my roarings are poured out like the waters.

3:25.web: For the thing which I fear comes on me, That which I am afraid of comes to me.
3:25.kjv: For the thing which I greatly feared is come upon me, and that which I was afraid of is come unto me.

3:26.web: I am not at ease, neither am I quiet, neither have I rest; but trouble comes.”
3:26.kjv: I was not in safety, neither had I rest, neither was I quiet; yet trouble came.

4:1.kjv: Then Eliphaz the Temanite answered and said,

4:2.web: “If someone ventures to talk with you, will you be grieved? But who can withhold himself from speaking?
4:2.kjv: If we assay to commune with thee, wilt thou be grieved? but who can withhold himself from speaking?

4:3.web: Behold, you have instructed many, you have strengthened the weak hands.
4:3.kjv: Behold, thou hast instructed many, and thou hast strengthened the weak hands.

4:4.web: Your words have supported him who was falling, You have made firm the feeble knees.
4:4.kjv: Thy words have upholden him that was falling, and thou hast strengthened the feeble knees.

4:5.web: But now it has come to you, and you faint. It touches you, and you are troubled.
4:5.kjv: But now it is come upon thee, and thou faintest; it toucheth thee, and thou art troubled.

4:6.web: Isn’t your piety your confidence? Isn’t the integrity of your ways your hope?
4:6.kjv: Is not this thy fear, thy confidence, thy hope, and the uprightness of thy ways?

4:7.web: “Remember, now, whoever perished, being innocent? Or where were the upright cut off?
4:7.kjv: Remember, I pray thee, who ever perished, being innocent? or where were the righteous cut off?

4:8.web: According to what I have seen, those who plow iniquity, and sow trouble, reap the same.
4:8.kjv: Even as I have seen, they that plow iniquity, and sow wickedness, reap the same.

4:9.web: By the breath of God they perish. By the blast of his anger are they consumed.
4:9.kjv: By the blast of God they perish, and by the breath of his nostrils are they consumed.

4:10.web: The roaring of the lion, and the voice of the fierce lion, the teeth of the young lions, are broken.
4:10.kjv: The roaring of the lion, and the voice of the fierce lion, and the teeth of the young lions, are broken.

4:11.web: The old lion perishes for lack of prey. The cubs of the lioness are scattered abroad.
4:11.kjv: The old lion perisheth for lack of prey, and the stout lion’s whelps are scattered abroad.

4:12.web: “Now a thing was secretly brought to me. My ear received a whisper of it.
4:12.kjv: Now a thing was secretly brought to me, and mine ear received a little thereof.

4:13.web: In thoughts from the visions of the night, when deep sleep falls on men,
4:13.kjv: In thoughts from the visions of the night, when deep sleep falleth on men,

4:14.web: fear came on me, and trembling, which made all my bones shake.
4:14.kjv: Fear came upon me, and trembling, which made all my bones to shake.

4:15.web: Then a spirit passed before my face. The hair of my flesh stood up.
4:15.kjv: Then a spirit passed before my face; the hair of my flesh stood up:

4:16.web: It stood still, but I couldn’t discern its appearance. A form was before my eyes. Silence, then I heard a voice, saying,
4:16.kjv: It stood still, but I could not discern the form thereof: an image was before mine eyes, there was silence, and I heard a voice, saying,

4:17.web: ‘Shall mortal man be more just than God? Shall a man be more pure than his Maker?
4:17.kjv: Shall mortal man be more just than God? shall a man be more pure than his maker?

4:18.web: Behold, he puts no trust in his servants. He charges his angels with error.
4:18.kjv: Behold, he put no trust in his servants; and his angels he charged with folly:

4:19.web: How much more, those who dwell in houses of clay, whose foundation is in the dust, who are crushed before the moth!
4:19.kjv: How much less in them that dwell in houses of clay, whose foundation is in the dust, which are crushed before the moth?

4:20.web: Between morning and evening they are destroyed. They perish forever without any regarding it.
4:20.kjv: They are destroyed from morning to evening: they perish for ever without any regarding it.

4:21.web: Isn’t their tent cord plucked up within them? They die, and that without wisdom.’
4:21.kjv: Doth not their excellency which is in them go away? they die, even without wisdom.

5:1.web: “Call now; is there any who will answer you? To which of the holy ones will you turn?
5:1.kjv: Call now, if there be any that will answer thee; and to which of the saints wilt thou turn?

5:2.web: For resentment kills the foolish man, and jealousy kills the simple.
5:2.kjv: For wrath killeth the foolish man, and envy slayeth the silly one.

5:3.web: I have seen the foolish taking root, but suddenly I cursed his habitation.
5:3.kjv: I have seen the foolish taking root: but suddenly I cursed his habitation.

5:4.web: His children are far from safety. They are crushed in the gate. Neither is there any to deliver them,
5:4.kjv: His children are far from safety, and they are crushed in the gate, neither is there any to deliver them.

5:5.web: whose harvest the hungry eats up, and take it even out of the thorns. The snare gapes for their substance.
5:5.kjv: Whose harvest the hungry eateth up, and taketh it even out of the thorns, and the robber swalloweth up their substance.

5:6.web: For affliction doesn’t come out of the dust, neither does trouble spring out of the ground;
5:6.kjv: Although affliction cometh not forth of the dust, neither doth trouble spring out of the ground;

5:7.web: but man is born to trouble, as the sparks fly upward.
5:7.kjv: Yet man is born unto trouble, as the sparks fly upward.

5:8.web: “But as for me, I would seek God. I would commit my cause to God,
5:8.kjv: I would seek unto God, and unto God would I commit my cause:

5:9.web: who does great things that can’t be fathomed, marvelous things without number;
5:9.kjv: Which doeth great things and unsearchable; marvellous things without number:

5:10.web: who gives rain on the earth, and sends waters on the fields;
5:10.kjv: Who giveth rain upon the earth, and sendeth waters upon the fields:

5:11.web: so that he sets up on high those who are low, those who mourn are exalted to safety.
5:11.kjv: To set up on high those that be low; that those which mourn may be exalted to safety.

5:12.web: He frustrates the plans of the crafty, So that their hands can’t perform their enterprise.
5:12.kjv: He disappointeth the devices of the crafty, so that their hands cannot perform their enterprise.

5:13.web: He takes the wise in their own craftiness; the counsel of the cunning is carried headlong.
5:13.kjv: He taketh the wise in their own craftiness: and the counsel of the froward is carried headlong.

5:14.web: They meet with darkness in the day time, and grope at noonday as in the night.
5:14.kjv: They meet with darkness in the daytime, and grope in the noonday as in the night.

5:15.web: But he saves from the sword of their mouth, even the needy from the hand of the mighty.
5:15.kjv: But he saveth the poor from the sword, from their mouth, and from the hand of the mighty.

5:16.web: So the poor has hope, and injustice shuts her mouth.
5:16.kjv: So the poor hath hope, and iniquity stoppeth her mouth.

5:17.web: “Behold, happy is the man whom God corrects. Therefore do not despise the chastening of the Almighty.
5:17.kjv: Behold, happy is the man whom God correcteth: therefore despise not thou the chastening of the Almighty:

5:18.web: For he wounds, and binds up. He injures, and his hands make whole.
5:18.kjv: For he maketh sore, and bindeth up: he woundeth, and his hands make whole.

5:19.web: He will deliver you in six troubles; yes, in seven no evil shall touch you.
5:19.kjv: He shall deliver thee in six troubles: yea, in seven there shall no evil touch thee.

5:20.web: In famine he will redeem you from death; in war, from the power of the sword.
5:20.kjv: In famine he shall redeem thee from death: and in war from the power of the sword.

5:21.web: You shall be hidden from the scourge of the tongue, neither shall you be afraid of destruction when it comes.
5:21.kjv: Thou shalt be hid from the scourge of the tongue: neither shalt thou be afraid of destruction when it cometh.

5:22.web: At destruction and famine you shall laugh, neither shall you be afraid of the animals of the earth.
5:22.kjv: At destruction and famine thou shalt laugh: neither shalt thou be afraid of the beasts of the earth.

bsb: of the field, and the wild
5:23.web: For you shall be allied with the stones of the field. The animals of the field shall be at peace with you.
5:23.kjv: For thou shalt be in league with the stones of the field: and the beasts of the field shall be at peace with thee.

5:24.web: You shall know that your tent is in peace. You shall visit your fold, and shall miss nothing.
5:24.kjv: And thou shalt know that thy tabernacle shall be in peace; and thou shalt visit thy habitation, and shalt not sin.

5:25.web: You shall know also that your offspring shall be great, Your offspring as the grass of the earth.
5:25.kjv: Thou shalt know also that thy seed shall be great, and thine offspring as the grass of the earth.

5:26.web: You shall come to your grave in a full age, like a shock of grain comes in its season.
5:26.kjv: Thou shalt come to thy grave in a full age, like as a shock of corn cometh in in his season.

5:27.web: Look this, we have searched it, so it is. Hear it, and know it for your good.”
5:27.kjv: Lo this, we have searched it, so it is; hear it, and know thou it for thy good.

6:2.web: “Oh that my anguish were weighed, and all my calamity laid in the balances!
6:2.kjv: O that my grief were throughly weighed, and my calamity laid in the balances together!

6:3.web: For now it would be heavier than the sand of the seas, therefore have my words been rash.
6:3.kjv: For now it would be heavier than the sand of the sea: therefore my words are swallowed up.

6:4.web: For the arrows of the Almighty are within me. My spirit drinks up their poison. The terrors of God set themselves in array against me.
6:4.kjv: For the arrows of the Almighty are within me, the poison whereof drinketh up my spirit: the terrors of God do set themselves in array against me.

6:5.web: Does the wild donkey bray when he has grass? Or does the ox low over his fodder?
6:5.kjv: Doth the wild ass bray when he hath grass? or loweth the ox over his fodder?

6:6.web: Can that which has no flavor be eaten without salt? Or is there any taste in the white of an egg?
6:6.kjv: Can that which is unsavoury be eaten without salt? or is there any taste in the white of an egg?

6:7.web: My soul refuses to touch them. They are as loathsome food to me.
6:7.kjv: The things that my soul refused to touch are as my sorrowful meat.

6:8.web: “Oh that I might have my request, that God would grant the thing that I long for,
6:8.kjv: Oh that I might have my request; and that God would grant me the thing that I long for!

6:9.web: even that it would please God to crush me; that he would let loose his hand, and cut me off!
6:9.kjv: Even that it would please God to destroy me; that he would let loose his hand, and cut me off!

6:10.web: Be it still my consolation, yes, let me exult in pain that doesn’t spare, that I have not denied the words of the Holy One.
6:10.kjv: Then should I yet have comfort; yea, I would harden myself in sorrow: let him not spare; for I have not concealed the words of the Holy One.

6:11.web: What is my strength, that I should wait? What is my end, that I should be patient?
6:11.kjv: What is my strength, that I should hope? and what is mine end, that I should prolong my life?

6:12.web: Is my strength the strength of stones? Or is my flesh of brass?
6:12.kjv: Is my strength the strength of stones? or is my flesh of brass?

6:13.web: Isn’t it that I have no help in me, That wisdom is driven quite from me?
6:13.kjv: Is not my help in me? and is wisdom driven quite from me?

6:14.web: “To him who is ready to faint, kindness should be shown from his friend; even to him who forsakes the fear of the Almighty.
6:14.kjv: To him that is afflicted pity should be shewed from his friend; but he forsaketh the fear of the Almighty.

6:15.web: My brothers have dealt deceitfully as a brook, as the channel of brooks that pass away;
6:15.kjv: My brethren have dealt deceitfully as a brook, and as the stream of brooks they pass away;

6:16.web: Which are black by reason of the ice, in which the snow hides itself.
6:16.kjv: Which are blackish by reason of the ice, and wherein the snow is hid:

6:17.web: In the dry season, they vanish. When it is hot, they are consumed out of their place.
6:17.kjv: What time they wax warm, they vanish: when it is hot, they are consumed out of their place.

6:18.web: The caravans that travel beside them turn away. They go up into the waste, and perish.
6:18.kjv: The paths of their way are turned aside; they go to nothing, and perish.

6:19.web: The caravans of Tema looked. The companies of Sheba waited for them.
6:19.kjv: The troops of Tema looked, the companies of Sheba waited for them.

6:20.web: They were distressed because they were confident. They came there, and were confounded.
6:20.kjv: They were confounded because they had hoped; they came thither, and were ashamed.

6:21.web: For now you are nothing. You see a terror, and are afraid.
6:21.kjv: For now ye are no thing; ye see my casting down, and are afraid.

6:22.web: Did I say, ‘Give to me?’ or, ‘Offer a present for me from your substance?’
6:22.kjv: Did I say, Bring unto me? or, Give a reward for me of your substance?

6:23.web: or, ‘Deliver me from the adversary’s hand?’ or, ‘Redeem me from the hand of the oppressors?’
6:23.kjv: Or, Deliver me from the enemy’s hand? or, Redeem me from the hand of the mighty?

6:24.web: “Teach me, and I will hold my peace. Cause me to understand wherein I have erred.
6:24.kjv: Teach me, and I will hold my tongue: and cause me to understand wherein I have erred.

6:25.web: How forcible are words of uprightness! But your reproof, what does it reprove?
6:25.kjv: How forcible are right words! but what doth your arguing reprove?

6:26.web: Do you intend to reprove words, since the speeches of one who is desperate are as wind?
6:26.kjv: Do ye imagine to reprove words, and the speeches of one that is desperate, which are as wind?

6:27.web: Yes, you would even cast lots for the fatherless, and make merchandise of your friend.
6:27.kjv: Yea, ye overwhelm the fatherless, and ye dig a pit for your friend.

6:28.web: Now therefore be pleased to look at me, for surely I shall not lie to your face.
6:28.kjv: Now therefore be content, look upon me; for it is evident unto you if I lie.

6:29.web: Please return. Let there be no injustice. Yes, return again. My cause is righteous.
6:29.kjv: Return, I pray you, let it not be iniquity; yea, return again, my righteousness is in it.

6:30.web: Is there injustice on my tongue? Can’t my taste discern mischievous things?
6:30.kjv: Is there iniquity in my tongue? cannot my taste discern perverse things?

bsb: Are not his days like those
7:1.web: “Isn’t a man forced to labor on earth? Aren’t his days like the days of a hired hand?
7:1.kjv: Is there not an appointed time to man upon earth? are not his days also like the days of an hireling?

7:2.web: As a servant who earnestly desires the shadow, as a hireling who looks for his wages,
7:2.kjv: As a servant earnestly desireth the shadow, and as an hireling looketh for the reward of his work:

7:3.web: so am I made to possess months of misery, wearisome nights are appointed to me.
7:3.kjv: So am I made to possess months of vanity, and wearisome nights are appointed to me.

7:4.web: When I lie down, I say, ‘When shall I arise, and the night be gone?’ I toss and turn until the dawning of the day.
7:4.kjv: When I lie down, I say, When shall I arise, and the night be gone? and I am full of tossings to and fro unto the dawning of the day.

7:5.web: My flesh is clothed with worms and clods of dust. My skin closes up, and breaks out afresh.
7:5.kjv: My flesh is clothed with worms and clods of dust; my skin is broken, and become loathsome.

7:6.web: My days are swifter than a weaver’s shuttle, and are spent without hope.
7:6.kjv: My days are swifter than a weaver’s shuttle, and are spent without hope.

7:7.web: Oh remember that my life is a breath. My eye shall no more see good.
7:7.kjv: O remember that my life is wind: mine eye shall no more see good.

bsb: but I will be no more.
7:8.web: The eye of him who sees me shall see me no more. Your eyes shall be on me, but I shall not be.
7:8.kjv: The eye of him that hath seen me shall see me no more: thine eyes are upon me, and I am not.

7:9.web: As the cloud is consumed and vanishes away, so he who goes down to Sheol shall come up no more.
7:9.kjv: As the cloud is consumed and vanisheth away: so he that goeth down to the grave shall come up no more.

7:10.web: He shall return no more to his house, neither shall his place know him any more.
7:10.kjv: He shall return no more to his house, neither shall his place know him any more.

7:11.web: “Therefore I will not keep silent. I will speak in the anguish of my spirit. I will complain in the bitterness of my soul.
7:11.kjv: Therefore I will not refrain my mouth; I will speak in the anguish of my spirit; I will complain in the bitterness of my soul.

7:12.web: Am I a sea, or a sea monster, that you put a guard over me?
7:12.kjv: Am I a sea, or a whale, that thou settest a watch over me?

7:13.web: When I say, ‘My bed shall comfort me. My couch shall ease my complaint;’
7:13.kjv: When I say, My bed shall comfort me, my couch shall ease my complaint;

7:14.web: then you scare me with dreams, and terrify me through visions:
7:14.kjv: Then thou scarest me with dreams, and terrifiest me through visions:

bsb: over my life in this body.
7:15.web: so that my soul chooses strangling, death rather than my bones.
7:15.kjv: So that my soul chooseth strangling, and death rather than my life.

7:16.web: I loathe my life. I don’t want to live forever. Leave me alone, for my days are but a breath.
7:16.kjv: I loathe it; I would not live alway: let me alone; for my days are vanity.

7:17.web: What is man, that you should magnify him, that you should set your mind on him,
7:17.kjv: What is man, that thou shouldest magnify him? and that thou shouldest set thine heart upon him?

7:18.web: that you should visit him every morning, and test him every moment?
7:18.kjv: And that thou shouldest visit him every morning, and try him every moment?

7:19.web: How long will you not look away from me, nor leave me alone until I swallow down my spittle?
7:19.kjv: How long wilt thou not depart from me, nor let me alone till I swallow down my spittle?

7:20.web: If I have sinned, what do I do to you, you watcher of men? Why have you set me as a mark for you, so that I am a burden to myself?
7:20.kjv: I have sinned; what shall I do unto thee, O thou preserver of men? why hast thou set me as a mark against thee, so that I am a burden to myself?

bsb: but I will be no more.”
7:21.web: Why do you not pardon my disobedience, and take away my iniquity? For now shall I lie down in the dust. You will seek me diligently, but I shall not be.”
7:21.kjv: And why dost thou not pardon my transgression, and take away mine iniquity? for now shall I sleep in the dust; and thou shalt seek me in the morning, but I shall not be.

8:1.kjv: Then answered Bildad the Shuhite, and said,

8:2.web: “How long will you speak these things? Shall the words of your mouth be a mighty wind?
8:2.kjv: How long wilt thou speak these things? and how long shall the words of thy mouth be like a strong wind?

8:3.web: Does God pervert justice? Or does the Almighty pervert righteousness?
8:3.kjv: Doth God pervert judgment? or doth the Almighty pervert justice?

8:4.web: If your children have sinned against him, He has delivered them into the hand of their disobedience.
8:4.kjv: If thy children have sinned against him, and he have cast them away for their transgression;

8:5.web: If you want to seek God diligently, make your supplication to the Almighty.
8:5.kjv: If thou wouldest seek unto God betimes, and make thy supplication to the Almighty;

8:6.web: If you were pure and upright, surely now he would awaken for you, and make the habitation of your righteousness prosperous.
8:6.kjv: If thou wert pure and upright; surely now he would awake for thee, and make the habitation of thy righteousness prosperous.

8:7.web: Though your beginning was small, yet your latter end would greatly increase.
8:7.kjv: Though thy beginning was small, yet thy latter end should greatly increase.

8:8.web: “Please inquire of past generations. Find out about the learning of their fathers.
8:8.kjv: For enquire, I pray thee, of the former age, and prepare thyself to the search of their fathers:

8:9.web: (For we are but of yesterday, and know nothing, because our days on earth are a shadow.)
8:9.kjv: (For we are but of yesterday, and know nothing, because our days upon earth are a shadow:)

8:10.web: Shall they not teach you, tell you, and utter words out of their heart?
8:10.kjv: Shall not they teach thee, and tell thee, and utter words out of their heart?

8:11.web: “Can the papyrus grow up without mire? Can the rushes grow without water?
8:11.kjv: Can the rush grow up without mire? can the flag grow without water?

8:12.web: While it is yet in its greenness, not cut down, it withers before any other reed.
8:12.kjv: Whilst it is yet in his greenness, and not cut down, it withereth before any other herb.

8:13.web: So are the paths of all who forget God. The hope of the godless man shall perish,
8:13.kjv: So are the paths of all that forget God; and the hypocrite’s hope shall perish:

8:14.web: Whose confidence shall break apart, Whose trust is a spider’s web.
8:14.kjv: Whose hope shall be cut off, and whose trust shall be a spider’s web.

8:15.web: He shall lean on his house, but it shall not stand. He shall cling to it, but it shall not endure.
8:15.kjv: He shall lean upon his house, but it shall not stand: he shall hold it fast, but it shall not endure.

8:16.web: He is green before the sun. His shoots go out along his garden.
8:16.kjv: He is green before the sun, and his branch shooteth forth in his garden.

8:17.web: His roots are wrapped around the rock pile. He sees the place of stones.
8:17.kjv: His roots are wrapped about the heap, and seeth the place of stones.

8:18.web: If he is destroyed from his place, then it shall deny him, saying, ‘I have not seen you.’
8:18.kjv: If he destroy him from his place, then it shall deny him, saying, I have not seen thee.

8:19.web: Behold, this is the joy of his way: out of the earth, others shall spring.
8:19.kjv: Behold, this is the joy of his way, and out of the earth shall others grow.

8:20.web: “Behold, God will not cast away a blameless man, neither will he uphold the evildoers.
8:20.kjv: Behold, God will not cast away a perfect man, neither will he help the evil doers:

8:21.web: He will still fill your mouth with laughter, your lips with shouting.
8:21.kjv: Till he fill thy mouth with laughing, and thy lips with rejoicing.

8:22.web: Those who hate you shall be clothed with shame. The tent of the wicked shall be no more.”
8:22.kjv: They that hate thee shall be clothed with shame; and the dwelling place of the wicked shall come to nought.

9:2.web: “Truly I know that it is so, but how can man be just with God?
9:2.kjv: I know it is so of a truth: but how should man be just with God?

9:3.web: If he is pleased to contend with him, he can’t answer him one time in a thousand.
9:3.kjv: If he will contend with him, he cannot answer him one of a thousand.

9:4.web: God who is wise in heart, and mighty in strength: who has hardened himself against him, and prospered?
9:4.kjv: He is wise in heart, and mighty in strength: who hath hardened himself against him, and hath prospered?

9:5.web: He removes the mountains, and they don’t know it, when he overturns them in his anger.
9:5.kjv: Which removeth the mountains, and they know not: which overturneth them in his anger.

9:6.web: He shakes the earth out of its place. Its pillars tremble.
9:6.kjv: Which shaketh the earth out of her place, and the pillars thereof tremble.

9:7.web: He commands the sun, and it doesn’t rise, and seals up the stars.
9:7.kjv: Which commandeth the sun, and it riseth not; and sealeth up the stars.

9:8.web: He alone stretches out the heavens, and treads on the waves of the sea.
9:8.kjv: Which alone spreadeth out the heavens, and treadeth upon the waves of the sea.

9:9.web: He makes the Bear, Orion, and the Pleiades, and the rooms of the south.
9:9.kjv: Which maketh Arcturus, Orion, and Pleiades, and the chambers of the south.

9:10.web: He does great things past finding out; yes, marvelous things without number.
9:10.kjv: Which doeth great things past finding out; yea, and wonders without number.

9:11.web: Behold, he goes by me, and I don’t see him. He passes on also, but I don’t perceive him.
9:11.kjv: Lo, he goeth by me, and I see him not: he passeth on also, but I perceive him not.

9:12.web: Behold, he snatches away. Who can hinder him? Who will ask him, ‘What are you doing?’
9:12.kjv: Behold, he taketh away, who can hinder him? who will say unto him, What doest thou?

9:13.web: “God will not withdraw his anger. The helpers of Rahab stoop under him.
9:13.kjv: If God will not withdraw his anger, the proud helpers do stoop under him.

9:14.web: How much less shall I answer him, And choose my words to argue with him?
9:14.kjv: How much less shall I answer him, and choose out my words to reason with him?

bsb: I could only beg my Judge
9:15.web: Though I were righteous, yet I wouldn’t answer him. I would make supplication to my judge.
9:15.kjv: Whom, though I were righteous, yet would I not answer, but I would make supplication to my judge.

9:16.web: If I had called, and he had answered me, yet I wouldn’t believe that he listened to my voice.
9:16.kjv: If I had called, and he had answered me; yet would I not believe that he had hearkened unto my voice.

9:17.web: For he breaks me with a storm, and multiplies my wounds without cause.
9:17.kjv: For he breaketh me with a tempest, and multiplieth my wounds without cause.

9:18.web: He will not allow me to catch my breath, but fills me with bitterness.
9:18.kjv: He will not suffer me to take my breath, but filleth me with bitterness.

bsb: it is a matter of strength,
it is a matter of justice,
9:19.web: If it is a matter of strength, behold, he is mighty! If of justice, ‘Who,’ says he, ‘will summon me?’
9:19.kjv: If I speak of strength, lo, he is strong: and if of judgment, who shall set me a time to plead?

9:20.web: Though I am righteous, my own mouth shall condemn me. Though I am blameless, it shall prove me perverse.
9:20.kjv: If I justify myself, mine own mouth shall condemn me: if I say, I am perfect, it shall also prove me perverse.

9:21.web: I am blameless. I don’t respect myself. I despise my life.
9:21.kjv: Though I were perfect, yet would I not know my soul: I would despise my life.

9:22.web: “It is all the same. Therefore I say he destroys the blameless and the wicked.
9:22.kjv: This is one thing, therefore I said it, He destroyeth the perfect and the wicked.

9:23.web: If the scourge kills suddenly, he will mock at the trial of the innocent.
9:23.kjv: If the scourge slay suddenly, he will laugh at the trial of the innocent.

9:24.web: The earth is given into the hand of the wicked. He covers the faces of its judges. If not he, then who is it?
9:24.kjv: The earth is given into the hand of the wicked: he covereth the faces of the judges thereof; if not, where, and who is he?

9:25.web: “Now my days are swifter than a runner. They flee away, they see no good.
9:25.kjv: Now my days are swifter than a post: they flee away, they see no good.

9:26.web: They have passed away as the swift ships, as the eagle that swoops on the prey.
9:26.kjv: They are passed away as the swift ships: as the eagle that hasteth to the prey.

9:27.web: If I say, ‘I will forget my complaint, I will put off my sad face, and cheer up;’
9:27.kjv: If I say, I will forget my complaint, I will leave off my heaviness, and comfort myself:

9:28.web: I am afraid of all my sorrows, I know that you will not hold me innocent.
9:28.kjv: I am afraid of all my sorrows, I know that thou wilt not hold me innocent.

9:29.web: I shall be condemned. Why then do I labor in vain?
9:29.kjv: If I be wicked, why then labour I in vain?

9:30.web: If I wash myself with snow, and cleanse my hands with lye,
9:30.kjv: If I wash myself with snow water, and make my hands never so clean;

9:31.web: yet you will plunge me in the ditch. My own clothes shall abhor me.
9:31.kjv: Yet shalt thou plunge me in the ditch, and mine own clothes shall abhor me.

9:32.web: For he is not a man, as I am, that I should answer him, that we should come together in judgment.
9:32.kjv: For he is not a man, as I am, that I should answer him, and we should come together in judgment.

9:33.web: There is no umpire between us, that might lay his hand on us both.
9:33.kjv: Neither is there any daysman betwixt us, that might lay his hand upon us both.

9:34.web: Let him take his rod away from me. Let his terror not make me afraid;
9:34.kjv: Let him take his rod away from me, and let not his fear terrify me:

9:35.web: then I would speak, and not fear him, for I am not so in myself.
9:35.kjv: Then would I speak, and not fear him; but it is not so with me.

10:1.web: “My soul is weary of my life. I will give free course to my complaint. I will speak in the bitterness of my soul.
10:1.kjv: My soul is weary of my life; I will leave my complaint upon myself; I will speak in the bitterness of my soul.

10:2.web: I will tell God, ‘Do not condemn me. Show me why you contend with me.
10:2.kjv: I will say unto God, Do not condemn me; shew me wherefore thou contendest with me.

10:3.web: Is it good to you that you should oppress, that you should despise the work of your hands, and smile on the counsel of the wicked?
10:3.kjv: Is it good unto thee that thou shouldest oppress, that thou shouldest despise the work of thine hands, and shine upon the counsel of the wicked?

10:4.web: Do you have eyes of flesh? Or do you see as man sees?
10:4.kjv: Hast thou eyes of flesh? or seest thou as man seeth?

10:5.web: Are your days as the days of mortals, or your years as man’s years,
10:5.kjv: Are thy days as the days of man? are thy years as man’s days,

10:6.web: that you inquire after my iniquity, and search after my sin?
10:6.kjv: That thou enquirest after mine iniquity, and searchest after my sin?

10:7.web: Although you know that I am not wicked, there is no one who can deliver out of your hand.
10:7.kjv: Thou knowest that I am not wicked; and there is none that can deliver out of thine hand.

10:8.web: “‘Your hands have framed me and fashioned me altogether, yet you destroy me.
10:8.kjv: Thine hands have made me and fashioned me together round about; yet thou dost destroy me.

10:9.web: Remember, I beg you, that you have fashioned me as clay. Will you bring me into dust again?
10:9.kjv: Remember, I beseech thee, that thou hast made me as the clay; and wilt thou bring me into dust again?

10:10.web: Haven’t you poured me out like milk, and curdled me like cheese?
10:10.kjv: Hast thou not poured me out as milk, and curdled me like cheese?

10:11.web: You have clothed me with skin and flesh, and knit me together with bones and sinews.
10:11.kjv: Thou hast clothed me with skin and flesh, and hast fenced me with bones and sinews.

10:12.web: You have granted me life and loving kindness. Your visitation has preserved my spirit.
10:12.kjv: Thou hast granted me life and favour, and thy visitation hath preserved my spirit.

10:13.web: Yet you hid these things in your heart. I know that this is with you:
10:13.kjv: And these things hast thou hid in thine heart: I know that this is with thee.

10:14.web: if I sin, then you mark me. You will not acquit me from my iniquity.
10:14.kjv: If I sin, then thou markest me, and thou wilt not acquit me from mine iniquity.

bsb: And even if I am righteous,
10:15.web: If I am wicked, woe to me. If I am righteous, I still shall not lift up my head, being filled with disgrace, and conscious of my affliction.
10:15.kjv: If I be wicked, woe unto me; and if I be righteous, yet will I not lift up my head. I am full of confusion; therefore see thou mine affliction;

bsb: Should I hold my head high,
10:16.web: If my head is held high, you hunt me like a lion. Again you show yourself powerful to me.
10:16.kjv: For it increaseth. Thou huntest me as a fierce lion: and again thou shewest thyself marvellous upon me.

10:17.web: You renew your witnesses against me, and increase your indignation on me. Changes and warfare are with me.
10:17.kjv: Thou renewest thy witnesses against me, and increasest thine indignation upon me; changes and war are against me.

10:18.web: “‘Why, then, have you brought me out of the womb? I wish I had given up the spirit, and no eye had seen me.
10:18.kjv: Wherefore then hast thou brought me forth out of the womb? Oh that I had given up the ghost, and no eye had seen me!

10:19.web: I should have been as though I had not been. I should have been carried from the womb to the grave.
10:19.kjv: I should have been as though I had not been; I should have been carried from the womb to the grave.

bsb: that I may have a little comfort,
10:20.web: Aren’t my days few? Cease then. Leave me alone, that I may find a little comfort,
10:20.kjv: Are not my days few? cease then, and let me alone, that I may take comfort a little,

10:21.web: before I go where I shall not return from, to the land of darkness and of the shadow of death;
10:21.kjv: Before I go whence I shall not return, even to the land of darkness and the shadow of death;

10:22.web: the land dark as midnight, of the shadow of death, without any order, where the light is as midnight.’”
10:22.kjv: A land of darkness, as darkness itself; and of the shadow of death, without any order, and where the light is as darkness.

11:1.kjv: Then answered Zophar the Naamathite, and said,

11:2.web: “Shouldn’t the multitude of words be answered? Should a man full of talk be justified?
11:2.kjv: Should not the multitude of words be answered? and should a man full of talk be justified?

11:3.web: Should your boastings make men hold their peace? When you mock, shall no man make you ashamed?
11:3.kjv: Should thy lies make men hold their peace? and when thou mockest, shall no man make thee ashamed?

11:4.web: For you say, ‘My doctrine is pure. I am clean in your eyes.’
11:4.kjv: For thou hast said, My doctrine is pure, and I am clean in thine eyes.

11:5.web: But oh that God would speak, and open his lips against you,
11:5.kjv: But oh that God would speak, and open his lips against thee;

11:6.web: that he would show you the secrets of wisdom! For true wisdom has two sides. Know therefore that God exacts of you less than your iniquity deserves.
11:6.kjv: And that he would shew thee the secrets of wisdom, that they are double to that which is! Know therefore that God exacteth of thee less than thine iniquity deserveth.

11:7.web: “Can you fathom the mystery of God? Or can you probe the limits of the Almighty?
11:7.kjv: Canst thou by searching find out God? canst thou find out the Almighty unto perfection?

11:8.web: They are high as heaven. What can you do? They are deeper than Sheol. What can you know?
11:8.kjv: It is as high as heaven; what canst thou do? deeper than hell; what canst thou know?

11:9.web: Its measure is longer than the earth, and broader than the sea.
11:9.kjv: The measure thereof is longer than the earth, and broader than the sea.

11:10.web: If he passes by, or confines, or convenes a court, then who can oppose him?
11:10.kjv: If he cut off, and shut up, or gather together, then who can hinder him?

11:11.web: For he knows false men. He sees iniquity also, even though he doesn’t consider it.
11:11.kjv: For he knoweth vain men: he seeth wickedness also; will he not then consider it?

11:12.web: An empty-headed man becomes wise when a man is born as a wild donkey’s colt.
11:12.kjv: For vain man would be wise, though man be born like a wild ass’s colt.

11:13.web: “If you set your heart aright, stretch out your hands toward him.
11:13.kjv: If thou prepare thine heart, and stretch out thine hands toward him;

11:14.web: If iniquity is in your hand, put it far away. Don’t let unrighteousness dwell in your tents.
11:14.kjv: If iniquity be in thine hand, put it far away, and let not wickedness dwell in thy tabernacles.

11:15.web: Surely then you shall lift up your face without spot; Yes, you shall be steadfast, and shall not fear:
11:15.kjv: For then shalt thou lift up thy face without spot; yea, thou shalt be stedfast, and shalt not fear:

11:16.web: for you shall forget your misery. You shall remember it like waters that have passed away.
11:16.kjv: Because thou shalt forget thy misery, and remember it as waters that pass away:

11:17.web: Life shall be clearer than the noonday. Though there is darkness, it shall be as the morning.
11:17.kjv: And thine age shall be clearer than the noonday; thou shalt shine forth, thou shalt be as the morning.

11:18.web: You shall be secure, because there is hope. Yes, you shall search, and shall take your rest in safety.
11:18.kjv: And thou shalt be secure, because there is hope; yea, thou shalt dig about thee, and thou shalt take thy rest in safety.

11:19.web: Also you shall lie down, and no one shall make you afraid. Yes, many shall court your favor.
11:19.kjv: Also thou shalt lie down, and none shall make thee afraid; yea, many shall make suit unto thee.

11:20.web: But the eyes of the wicked shall fail. They shall have no way to flee. Their hope shall be the giving up of the spirit.”
11:20.kjv: But the eyes of the wicked shall fail, and they shall not escape, and their hope shall be as the giving up of the ghost.

12:2.web: “No doubt, but you are the people, and wisdom shall die with you.
12:2.kjv: No doubt but ye are the people, and wisdom shall die with you.

12:3.web: But I have understanding as well as you; I am not inferior to you. Yes, who doesn’t know such things as these?
12:3.kjv: But I have understanding as well as you; I am not inferior to you: yea, who knoweth not such things as these?

12:4.web: I am like one who is a joke to his neighbor, I, who called on God, and he answered. The just, the blameless man is a joke.
12:4.kjv: I am as one mocked of his neighbour, who calleth upon God, and he answereth him: the just upright man is laughed to scorn.

12:5.web: In the thought of him who is at ease there is contempt for misfortune. It is ready for them whose foot slips.
12:5.kjv: He that is ready to slip with his feet is as a lamp despised in the thought of him that is at ease.

12:6.web: The tents of robbers prosper. Those who provoke God are secure, who carry their God in their hands.
12:6.kjv: The tabernacles of robbers prosper, and they that provoke God are secure; into whose hand God bringeth abundantly.

12:7.web: “But ask the animals, now, and they shall teach you; the birds of the sky, and they shall tell you.
12:7.kjv: But ask now the beasts, and they shall teach thee; and the fowls of the air, and they shall tell thee:

12:8.web: Or speak to the earth, and it shall teach you. The fish of the sea shall declare to you.
12:8.kjv: Or speak to the earth, and it shall teach thee: and the fishes of the sea shall declare unto thee.

12:9.web: Who doesn’t know that in all these, Yahweh’s hand has done this,
12:9.kjv: Who knoweth not in all these that the hand of the LORD hath wrought this?

12:10.web: in whose hand is the life of every living thing, and the breath of all mankind?
12:10.kjv: In whose hand is the soul of every living thing, and the breath of all mankind.

12:11.web: Doesn’t the ear try words, even as the palate tastes its food?
12:11.kjv: Doth not the ear try words? and the mouth taste his meat?

12:12.web: With aged men is wisdom, in length of days understanding.
12:12.kjv: With the ancient is wisdom; and in length of days understanding.

12:13.web: “With God is wisdom and might. He has counsel and understanding.
12:13.kjv: With him is wisdom and strength, he hath counsel and understanding.

12:14.web: Behold, he breaks down, and it can’t be built again. He imprisons a man, and there can be no release.
12:14.kjv: Behold, he breaketh down, and it cannot be built again: he shutteth up a man, and there can be no opening.

12:15.web: Behold, he withholds the waters, and they dry up. Again, he sends them out, and they overturn the earth.
12:15.kjv: Behold, he withholdeth the waters, and they dry up: also he sendeth them out, and they overturn the earth.

12:16.web: With him is strength and wisdom. The deceived and the deceiver are his.
12:16.kjv: With him is strength and wisdom: the deceived and the deceiver are his.

12:17.web: He leads counselors away stripped. He makes judges fools.
12:17.kjv: He leadeth counsellors away spoiled, and maketh the judges fools.

12:18.web: He loosens the bond of kings. He binds their waist with a belt.
12:18.kjv: He looseth the bond of kings, and girdeth their loins with a girdle.

12:19.web: He leads priests away stripped, and overthrows the mighty.
12:19.kjv: He leadeth princes away spoiled, and overthroweth the mighty.

12:20.web: He removes the speech of those who are trusted, and takes away the understanding of the elders.
12:20.kjv: He removeth away the speech of the trusty, and taketh away the understanding of the aged.

12:21.web: He pours contempt on princes, and loosens the belt of the strong.
12:21.kjv: He poureth contempt upon princes, and weakeneth the strength of the mighty.

12:22.web: He uncovers deep things out of darkness, and brings out to light the shadow of death.
12:22.kjv: He discovereth deep things out of darkness, and bringeth out to light the shadow of death.

12:23.web: He increases the nations, and he destroys them. He enlarges the nations, and he leads them captive.
12:23.kjv: He increaseth the nations, and destroyeth them: he enlargeth the nations, and straiteneth them again.

12:24.web: He takes away understanding from the chiefs of the people of the earth, and causes them to wander in a wilderness where there is no way.
12:24.kjv: He taketh away the heart of the chief of the people of the earth, and causeth them to wander in a wilderness where there is no way.

12:25.web: They grope in the dark without light. He makes them stagger like a drunken man.
12:25.kjv: They grope in the dark without light, and he maketh them to stagger like a drunken man.

13:1.web: “Behold, my eye has seen all this. My ear has heard and understood it.
13:1.kjv: Lo, mine eye hath seen all this, mine ear hath heard and understood it.

13:2.web: What you know, I know also. I am not inferior to you.
13:2.kjv: What ye know, the same do I know also: I am not inferior unto you.

13:3.web: “Surely I would speak to the Almighty. I desire to reason with God.
13:3.kjv: Surely I would speak to the Almighty, and I desire to reason with God.

13:4.web: But you are forgers of lies. You are all physicians of no value.
13:4.kjv: But ye are forgers of lies, ye are all physicians of no value.

13:5.web: Oh that you would be completely silent! Then you would be wise.
13:5.kjv: Oh that ye would altogether hold your peace! and it should be your wisdom.

13:6.web: Hear now my reasoning. Listen to the pleadings of my lips.
13:6.kjv: Hear now my reasoning, and hearken to the pleadings of my lips.

13:7.web: Will you speak unrighteously for God, and talk deceitfully for him?
13:7.kjv: Will ye speak wickedly for God? and talk deceitfully for him?

13:8.web: Will you show partiality to him? Will you contend for God?
13:8.kjv: Will ye accept his person? will ye contend for God?

13:9.web: Is it good that he should search you out? Or as one deceives a man, will you deceive him?
13:9.kjv: Is it good that he should search you out? or as one man mocketh another, do ye so mock him?

13:10.web: He will surely reprove you, if you secretly show partiality.
13:10.kjv: He will surely reprove you, if ye do secretly accept persons.

13:11.web: Shall not his majesty make you afraid, And his dread fall on you?
13:11.kjv: Shall not his excellency make you afraid? and his dread fall upon you?

13:12.web: Your memorable sayings are proverbs of ashes, Your defenses are defenses of clay.
13:12.kjv: Your remembrances are like unto ashes, your bodies to bodies of clay.

13:13.web: “Be silent, leave me alone, that I may speak. Let come on me what will.
13:13.kjv: Hold your peace, let me alone, that I may speak, and let come on me what will.

13:14.web: Why should I take my flesh in my teeth, and put my life in my hand?
13:14.kjv: Wherefore do I take my flesh in my teeth, and put my life in mine hand?

13:15.web: Behold, he will kill me. I have no hope. Nevertheless, I will maintain my ways before him.
13:15.kjv: Though he slay me, yet will I trust in him: but I will maintain mine own ways before him.

13:16.web: This also shall be my salvation, that a godless man shall not come before him.
13:16.kjv: He also shall be my salvation: for an hypocrite shall not come before him.

13:17.web: Hear diligently my speech. Let my declaration be in your ears.
13:17.kjv: Hear diligently my speech, and my declaration with your ears.

13:18.web: See now, I have set my cause in order. I know that I am righteous.
13:18.kjv: Behold now, I have ordered my cause; I know that I shall be justified.

13:19.web: Who is he who will contend with me? For then would I hold my peace and give up the spirit.
13:19.kjv: Who is he that will plead with me? for now, if I hold my tongue, I shall give up the ghost.

13:20.web: “Only don’t do two things to me; then I will not hide myself from your face:
13:20.kjv: Only do not two things unto me: then will I not hide myself from thee.

13:21.web: withdraw your hand far from me; and don’t let your terror make me afraid.
13:21.kjv: Withdraw thine hand far from me: and let not thy dread make me afraid.

13:22.web: Then call, and I will answer; or let me speak, and you answer me.
13:22.kjv: Then call thou, and I will answer: or let me speak, and answer thou me.

13:23.web: How many are my iniquities and sins? Make me know my disobedience and my sin.
13:23.kjv: How many are mine iniquities and sins? make me to know my transgression and my sin.

13:24.web: Why hide you your face, and hold me for your enemy?
13:24.kjv: Wherefore hidest thou thy face, and holdest me for thine enemy?

13:25.web: Will you harass a driven leaf? Will you pursue the dry stubble?
13:25.kjv: Wilt thou break a leaf driven to and fro? and wilt thou pursue the dry stubble?

13:26.web: For you write bitter things against me, and make me inherit the iniquities of my youth:
13:26.kjv: For thou writest bitter things against me, and makest me to possess the iniquities of my youth.

13:27.web: You also put my feet in the stocks, and mark all my paths. You set a bound to the soles of my feet,
13:27.kjv: Thou puttest my feet also in the stocks, and lookest narrowly unto all my paths; thou settest a print upon the heels of my feet.

13:28.web: though I am decaying like a rotten thing, like a garment that is moth-eaten.
13:28.kjv: And he, as a rotten thing, consumeth, as a garment that is moth eaten.

14:1.web: “Man, who is born of a woman, is of few days, and full of trouble.
14:1.kjv: Man that is born of a woman is of few days, and full of trouble.

14:2.web: He grows up like a flower, and is cut down. He also flees like a shadow, and doesn’t continue.
14:2.kjv: He cometh forth like a flower, and is cut down: he fleeth also as a shadow, and continueth not.

14:3.web: Do you open your eyes on such a one, and bring me into judgment with you?
14:3.kjv: And dost thou open thine eyes upon such an one, and bringest me into judgment with thee?

14:4.web: Who can bring a clean thing out of an unclean? Not one.
14:4.kjv: Who can bring a clean thing out of an unclean? not one.

14:5.web: Seeing his days are determined, the number of his months is with you, and you have appointed his bounds that he can’t pass;
14:5.kjv: Seeing his days are determined, the number of his months are with thee, thou hast appointed his bounds that he cannot pass;

14:6.web: Look away from him, that he may rest, until he shall accomplish, as a hireling, his day.
14:6.kjv: Turn from him, that he may rest, till he shall accomplish, as an hireling, his day.

14:7.web: “For there is hope for a tree, If it is cut down, that it will sprout again, that the tender branch of it will not cease.
14:7.kjv: For there is hope of a tree, if it be cut down, that it will sprout again, and that the tender branch thereof will not cease.

14:8.web: Though its root grows old in the earth, and its stock dies in the ground,
14:8.kjv: Though the root thereof wax old in the earth, and the stock thereof die in the ground;

14:9.web: yet through the scent of water it will bud, and sprout boughs like a plant.
14:9.kjv: Yet through the scent of water it will bud, and bring forth boughs like a plant.

14:10.web: But man dies, and is laid low. Yes, man gives up the spirit, and where is he?
14:10.kjv: But man dieth, and wasteth away: yea, man giveth up the ghost, and where is he?

14:11.web: As the waters fail from the sea, and the river wastes and dries up,
14:11.kjv: As the waters fail from the sea, and the flood decayeth and drieth up:

14:12.web: so man lies down and doesn’t rise. Until the heavens are no more, they shall not awake, nor be roused out of their sleep.
14:12.kjv: So man lieth down, and riseth not: till the heavens be no more, they shall not awake, nor be raised out of their sleep.

14:13.web: “Oh that you would hide me in Sheol, that you would keep me secret, until your wrath is past, that you would appoint me a set time, and remember me!
14:13.kjv: Oh that thou wouldest hide me in the grave, that thou wouldest keep me secret, until thy wrath be past, that thou wouldest appoint me a set time, and remember me!

14:14.web: If a man dies, shall he live again? All the days of my warfare would I wait, until my release should come.
14:14.kjv: If a man die, shall he live again? all the days of my appointed time will I wait, till my change come.

14:15.web: You would call, and I would answer you. You would have a desire to the work of your hands.
14:15.kjv: Thou shalt call, and I will answer thee: thou wilt have a desire to the work of thine hands.

14:16.web: But now you count my steps. Don’t you watch over my sin?
14:16.kjv: For now thou numberest my steps: dost thou not watch over my sin?

14:17.web: My disobedience is sealed up in a bag. You fasten up my iniquity.
14:17.kjv: My transgression is sealed up in a bag, and thou sewest up mine iniquity.

14:18.web: “But the mountain falling comes to nothing. The rock is removed out of its place;
14:18.kjv: And surely the mountain falling cometh to nought, and the rock is removed out of his place.

14:19.web: The waters wear the stones. The torrents of it wash away the dust of the earth. So you destroy the hope of man.
14:19.kjv: The waters wear the stones: thou washest away the things which grow out of the dust of the earth; and thou destroyest the hope of man.

14:20.web: You forever prevail against him, and he departs. You change his face, and send him away.
14:20.kjv: Thou prevailest for ever against him, and he passeth: thou changest his countenance, and sendest him away.

14:21.web: His sons come to honor, and he doesn’t know it. They are brought low, but he doesn’t perceive it of them.
14:21.kjv: His sons come to honour, and he knoweth it not; and they are brought low, but he perceiveth it not of them.

14:22.web: But his flesh on him has pain, and his soul within him mourns.”
14:22.kjv: But his flesh upon him shall have pain, and his soul within him shall mourn.

15:1.kjv: Then answered Eliphaz the Temanite, and said,

15:2.web: “Should a wise man answer with vain knowledge, and fill himself with the east wind?
15:2.kjv: Should a wise man utter vain knowledge, and fill his belly with the east wind?

15:3.web: Should he reason with unprofitable talk, or with speeches with which he can do no good?
15:3.kjv: Should he reason with unprofitable talk? or with speeches wherewith he can do no good?

15:4.web: Yes, you do away with fear, and hinder devotion before God.
15:4.kjv: Yea, thou castest off fear, and restrainest prayer before God.

15:5.web: For your iniquity teaches your mouth, and you choose the language of the crafty.
15:5.kjv: For thy mouth uttereth thine iniquity, and thou choosest the tongue of the crafty.

15:6.web: Your own mouth condemns you, and not I. Yes, your own lips testify against you.
15:6.kjv: Thine own mouth condemneth thee, and not I: yea, thine own lips testify against thee.

15:7.web: “Are you the first man who was born? Or were you brought out before the hills?
15:7.kjv: Art thou the first man that was born? or wast thou made before the hills?

15:8.web: Have you heard the secret counsel of God? Do you limit wisdom to yourself?
15:8.kjv: Hast thou heard the secret of God? and dost thou restrain wisdom to thyself?

15:9.web: What do you know, that we don’t know? What do you understand, which is not in us?
15:9.kjv: What knowest thou, that we know not? what understandest thou, which is not in us?

15:10.web: With us are both the gray-headed and the very aged men, much elder than your father.
15:10.kjv: With us are both the grayheaded and very aged men, much elder than thy father.

15:11.web: Are the consolations of God too small for you, even the word that is gentle toward you?
15:11.kjv: Are the consolations of God small with thee? is there any secret thing with thee?

15:12.web: Why does your heart carry you away? Why do your eyes flash,
15:12.kjv: Why doth thine heart carry thee away? and what do thy eyes wink at,

15:13.web: That you turn your spirit against God, and let such words go out of your mouth?
15:13.kjv: That thou turnest thy spirit against God, and lettest such words go out of thy mouth?

15:14.web: What is man, that he should be clean? What is he who is born of a woman, that he should be righteous?
15:14.kjv: What is man, that he should be clean? and he which is born of a woman, that he should be righteous?

15:15.web: Behold, he puts no trust in his holy ones. Yes, the heavens are not clean in his sight;
15:15.kjv: Behold, he putteth no trust in his saints; yea, the heavens are not clean in his sight.

15:16.web: how much less one who is abominable and corrupt, a man who drinks iniquity like water!
15:16.kjv: How much more abominable and filthy is man, which drinketh iniquity like water?

15:17.web: “I will show you, listen to me; that which I have seen I will declare
15:17.kjv: I will shew thee, hear me; and that which I have seen I will declare;

15:18.web: (which wise men have told by their fathers, and have not hidden it;
15:18.kjv: Which wise men have told from their fathers, and have not hid it:

15:19.web: to whom alone the land was given, and no stranger passed among them):
15:19.kjv: Unto whom alone the earth was given, and no stranger passed among them.

15:20.web: the wicked man writhes in pain all his days, even the number of years that are laid up for the oppressor.
15:20.kjv: The wicked man travaileth with pain all his days, and the number of years is hidden to the oppressor.

15:21.web: A sound of terrors is in his ears. In prosperity the destroyer shall come on him.
15:21.kjv: A dreadful sound is in his ears: in prosperity the destroyer shall come upon him.

15:22.web: He doesn’t believe that he shall return out of darkness. He is waited for by the sword.
15:22.kjv: He believeth not that he shall return out of darkness, and he is waited for of the sword.

15:23.web: He wanders abroad for bread, saying, ‘Where is it?’ He knows that the day of darkness is ready at his hand.
15:23.kjv: He wandereth abroad for bread, saying, Where is it? he knoweth that the day of darkness is ready at his hand.

15:24.web: Distress and anguish make him afraid. They prevail against him, as a king ready to the battle.
15:24.kjv: Trouble and anguish shall make him afraid; they shall prevail against him, as a king ready to the battle.

15:25.web: Because he has stretched out his hand against God, and behaves himself proudly against the Almighty;
15:25.kjv: For he stretcheth out his hand against God, and strengtheneth himself against the Almighty.

15:26.web: he runs at him with a stiff neck, with the thick shields of his bucklers;
15:26.kjv: He runneth upon him, even on his neck, upon the thick bosses of his bucklers:

15:27.web: because he has covered his face with his fatness, and gathered fat on his thighs.
15:27.kjv: Because he covereth his face with his fatness, and maketh collops of fat on his flanks.

15:28.web: He has lived in desolate cities, in houses which no one inhabited, which were ready to become heaps.
15:28.kjv: And he dwelleth in desolate cities, and in houses which no man inhabiteth, which are ready to become heaps.

15:29.web: He shall not be rich, neither shall his substance continue, neither shall their possessions be extended on the earth.
15:29.kjv: He shall not be rich, neither shall his substance continue, neither shall he prolong the perfection thereof upon the earth.

15:30.web: He shall not depart out of darkness. The flame shall dry up his branches. By the breath of God’s mouth shall he go away.
15:30.kjv: He shall not depart out of darkness; the flame shall dry up his branches, and by the breath of his mouth shall he go away.

15:31.web: Let him not trust in emptiness, deceiving himself; for emptiness shall be his reward.
15:31.kjv: Let not him that is deceived trust in vanity: for vanity shall be his recompence.

bsb: It will be paid in full
15:32.web: It shall be accomplished before his time. His branch shall not be green.
15:32.kjv: It shall be accomplished before his time, and his branch shall not be green.

bsb: He will be like a vine
15:33.web: He shall shake off his unripe grape as the vine, and shall cast off his flower as the olive tree.
15:33.kjv: He shall shake off his unripe grape as the vine, and shall cast off his flower as the olive.

15:34.web: For the company of the godless shall be barren, and fire shall consume the tents of bribery.
15:34.kjv: For the congregation of hypocrites shall be desolate, and fire shall consume the tabernacles of bribery.

15:35.web: They conceive mischief, and produce iniquity. Their heart prepares deceit.”
15:35.kjv: They conceive mischief, and bring forth vanity, and their belly prepareth deceit.

16:2.web: “I have heard many such things. You are all miserable comforters!
16:2.kjv: I have heard many such things: miserable comforters are ye all.

16:3.web: Shall vain words have an end? Or what provokes you that you answer?
16:3.kjv: Shall vain words have an end? or what emboldeneth thee that thou answerest?

16:4.web: I also could speak as you do. If your soul were in my soul’s place, I could join words together against you, and shake my head at you,
16:4.kjv: I also could speak as ye do: if your soul were in my soul’s stead, I could heap up words against you, and shake mine head at you.

16:5.web: but I would strengthen you with my mouth. The solace of my lips would relieve you.
16:5.kjv: But I would strengthen you with my mouth, and the moving of my lips should asswage your grief.

16:6.web: “Though I speak, my grief is not subsided. Though I forbear, what am I eased?
16:6.kjv: Though I speak, my grief is not asswaged: and though I forbear, what am I eased?

16:7.web: But now, God, you have surely worn me out. You have made desolate all my company.
16:7.kjv: But now he hath made me weary: thou hast made desolate all my company.

16:8.web: You have shriveled me up. This is a witness against me. My leanness rises up against me. It testifies to my face.
16:8.kjv: And thou hast filled me with wrinkles, which is a witness against me: and my leanness rising up in me beareth witness to my face.

16:9.web: He has torn me in his wrath, and persecuted me. He has gnashed on me with his teeth. My adversary sharpens his eyes on me.
16:9.kjv: He teareth me in his wrath, who hateth me: he gnasheth upon me with his teeth; mine enemy sharpeneth his eyes upon me.

16:10.web: They have gaped on me with their mouth. They have struck me on the cheek reproachfully. They gather themselves together against me.
16:10.kjv: They have gaped upon me with their mouth; they have smitten me upon the cheek reproachfully; they have gathered themselves together against me.

16:11.web: God delivers me to the ungodly, and casts me into the hands of the wicked.
16:11.kjv: God hath delivered me to the ungodly, and turned me over into the hands of the wicked.

16:12.web: I was at ease, and he broke me apart. Yes, he has taken me by the neck, and dashed me to pieces. He has also set me up for his target.
16:12.kjv: I was at ease, but he hath broken me asunder: he hath also taken me by my neck, and shaken me to pieces, and set me up for his mark.

16:13.web: His archers surround me. He splits my kidneys apart, and does not spare. He pours out my gall on the ground.
16:13.kjv: His archers compass me round about, he cleaveth my reins asunder, and doth not spare; he poureth out my gall upon the ground.

16:14.web: He breaks me with breach on breach. He runs on me like a giant.
16:14.kjv: He breaketh me with breach upon breach, he runneth upon me like a giant.

16:15.web: I have sewed sackcloth on my skin, and have thrust my horn in the dust.
16:15.kjv: I have sewed sackcloth upon my skin, and defiled my horn in the dust.

16:16.web: My face is red with weeping. Deep darkness is on my eyelids.
16:16.kjv: My face is foul with weeping, and my eyelids is the shadow of death;

16:17.web: Although there is no violence in my hands, and my prayer is pure.
16:17.kjv: Not for any injustice in mine hands: also my prayer is pure.

16:18.web: “Earth, don’t cover my blood. Let my cry have no place to rest.
16:18.kjv: O earth, cover not thou my blood, and let my cry have no place.

16:19.web: Even now, behold, my witness is in heaven. He who vouches for me is on high.
16:19.kjv: Also now, behold, my witness is in heaven, and my record is on high.

16:20.web: My friends scoff at me. My eyes pour out tears to God,
16:20.kjv: My friends scorn me: but mine eye poureth out tears unto God.

16:21.web: that he would maintain the right of a man with God, of a son of man with his neighbor!
16:21.kjv: Oh that one might plead for a man with God, as a man pleadeth for his neighbour!

16:22.web: For when a few years have come, I shall go the way of no return.
16:22.kjv: When a few years are come, then I shall go the way whence I shall not return.

17:1.web: “My spirit is consumed. My days are extinct, And the grave is ready for me.
17:1.kjv: My breath is corrupt, my days are extinct, the graves are ready for me.

17:2.web: Surely there are mockers with me. My eye dwells on their provocation.
17:2.kjv: Are there not mockers with me? and doth not mine eye continue in their provocation?

17:3.web: “Now give a pledge, be collateral for me with yourself. Who is there who will strike hands with me?
17:3.kjv: Lay down now, put me in a surety with thee; who is he that will strike hands with me?

17:4.web: For you have hidden their heart from understanding, Therefore you shall not exalt them.
17:4.kjv: For thou hast hid their heart from understanding: therefore shalt thou not exalt them.

17:5.web: He who denounces his friends for plunder, Even the eyes of his children shall fail.
17:5.kjv: He that speaketh flattery to his friends, even the eyes of his children shall fail.

17:6.web: “But he has made me a byword of the people. They spit in my face.
