34:6.kjv: Should I lie against my right? my wound is incurable without transgression.

34:7.web: What man is like Job, who drinks scorn like water,
34:7.kjv: What man is like Job, who drinketh up scorning like water?

34:8.web: Who goes in company with the workers of iniquity, and walks with wicked men?
34:8.kjv: Which goeth in company with the workers of iniquity, and walketh with wicked men.

34:9.web: For he has said, ‘It profits a man nothing that he should delight himself with God.’
34:9.kjv: For he hath said, It profiteth a man nothing that he should delight himself with God.

34:10.web: “Therefore listen to me, you men of understanding: far be it from God, that he should do wickedness, from the Almighty, that he should commit iniquity.
34:10.kjv: Therefore hearken unto me, ye men of understanding: far be it from God, that he should do wickedness; and from the Almighty, that he should commit iniquity.

34:11.web: For the work of a man he will render to him, and cause every man to find according to his ways.
34:11.kjv: For the work of a man shall he render unto him, and cause every man to find according to his ways.

34:12.web: Yes surely, God will not do wickedly, neither will the Almighty pervert justice.
34:12.kjv: Yea, surely God will not do wickedly, neither will the Almighty pervert judgment.

34:13.web: Who put him in charge of the earth? or who has appointed him over the whole world?
34:13.kjv: Who hath given him a charge over the earth? or who hath disposed the whole world?

34:14.web: If he set his heart on himself, If he gathered to himself his spirit and his breath,
34:14.kjv: If he set his heart upon man, if he gather unto himself his spirit and his breath;

34:15.web: all flesh would perish together, and man would turn again to dust.
34:15.kjv: All flesh shall perish together, and man shall turn again unto dust.

34:16.web: “If now you have understanding, hear this. Listen to the voice of my words.
34:16.kjv: If now thou hast understanding, hear this: hearken to the voice of my words.

34:17.web: Shall even one who hates justice govern? Will you condemn him who is righteous and mighty?—
34:17.kjv: Shall even he that hateth right govern? and wilt thou condemn him that is most just?

34:18.web: Who says to a king, ‘Vile!’ or to nobles, ‘Wicked!’?
34:18.kjv: Is it fit to say to a king, Thou art wicked? and to princes, Ye are ungodly?

34:19.web: Who doesn’t respect the persons of princes, nor respects the rich more than the poor; for they all are the work of his hands.
34:19.kjv: How much less to him that accepteth not the persons of princes, nor regardeth the rich more than the poor? for they all are the work of his hands.

34:20.web: In a moment they die, even at midnight. The people are shaken and pass away. The mighty are taken away without a hand.
34:20.kjv: In a moment shall they die, and the people shall be troubled at midnight, and pass away: and the mighty shall be taken away without hand.

34:21.web: “For his eyes are on the ways of a man. He sees all his goings.
34:21.kjv: For his eyes are upon the ways of man, and he seeth all his goings.

34:22.web: There is no darkness, nor thick gloom, where the workers of iniquity may hide themselves.
34:22.kjv: There is no darkness, nor shadow of death, where the workers of iniquity may hide themselves.

34:23.web: For he doesn’t need to consider a man further, that he should go before God in judgment.
34:23.kjv: For he will not lay upon man more than right; that he should enter into judgment with God.

34:24.web: He breaks in pieces mighty men in ways past finding out, and sets others in their place.
34:24.kjv: He shall break in pieces mighty men without number, and set others in their stead.

34:25.web: Therefore he takes knowledge of their works. He overturns them in the night, so that they are destroyed.
34:25.kjv: Therefore he knoweth their works, and he overturneth them in the night, so that they are destroyed.

34:26.web: He strikes them as wicked men in the open sight of others;
34:26.kjv: He striketh them as wicked men in the open sight of others;

34:27.web: because they turned away from following him, and wouldn’t pay attention to any of his ways,
34:27.kjv: Because they turned back from him, and would not consider any of his ways:

34:28.web: so that they caused the cry of the poor to come to him. He heard the cry of the afflicted.
34:28.kjv: So that they cause the cry of the poor to come unto him, and he heareth the cry of the afflicted.

34:29.web: When he gives quietness, who then can condemn? When he hides his face, who then can see him? Alike whether to a nation, or to a man,
34:29.kjv: When he giveth quietness, who then can make trouble? and when he hideth his face, who then can behold him? whether it be done against a nation, or against a man only:

34:30.web: that the godless man may not reign, that there be no one to ensnare the people.
34:30.kjv: That the hypocrite reign not, lest the people be ensnared.

34:31.web: “For has any said to God, ‘I am guilty, but I will not offend any more.
34:31.kjv: Surely it is meet to be said unto God, I have borne chastisement, I will not offend any more:

34:32.web: Teach me that which I don’t see. If I have done iniquity, I will do it no more’?
34:32.kjv: That which I see not teach thou me: if I have done iniquity, I will do no more.

34:33.web: Shall his recompense be as you desire, that you refuse it? For you must choose, and not I. Therefore speak what you know.
34:33.kjv: Should it be according to thy mind? he will recompense it, whether thou refuse, or whether thou choose; and not I: therefore speak what thou knowest.

34:34.web: Men of understanding will tell me, yes, every wise man who hears me:
34:34.kjv: Let men of understanding tell me, and let a wise man hearken unto me.

34:35.web: ‘Job speaks without knowledge. His words are without wisdom.’
34:35.kjv: Job hath spoken without knowledge, and his words were without wisdom.

34:36.web: I wish that Job were tried to the end, because of his answering like wicked men.
34:36.kjv: My desire is that Job may be tried unto the end because of his answers for wicked men.

34:37.web: For he adds rebellion to his sin. He claps his hands among us, and multiplies his words against God.”
34:37.kjv: For he addeth rebellion unto his sin, he clappeth his hands among us, and multiplieth his words against God.

35:2.web: “Do you think this to be your right, or do you say, ‘My righteousness is more than God’s,’
35:2.kjv: Thinkest thou this to be right, that thou saidst, My righteousness is more than God’s?

35:3.web: That you ask, ‘What advantage will it be to you? What profit shall I have, more than if I had sinned?’
35:3.kjv: For thou saidst, What advantage will it be unto thee? and, What profit shall I have, if I be cleansed from my sin?

35:4.web: I will answer you, and your companions with you.
35:4.kjv: I will answer thee, and thy companions with thee.

35:5.web: Look to the heavens, and see. See the skies, which are higher than you.
35:5.kjv: Look unto the heavens, and see; and behold the clouds which are higher than thou.

35:6.web: If you have sinned, what effect do you have against him? If your transgressions are multiplied, what do you do to him?
35:6.kjv: If thou sinnest, what doest thou against him? or if thy transgressions be multiplied, what doest thou unto him?

35:7.web: If you are righteous, what do you give him? Or what does he receive from your hand?
35:7.kjv: If thou be righteous, what givest thou him? or what receiveth he of thine hand?

35:8.web: Your wickedness may hurt a man as you are, and your righteousness may profit a son of man.
35:8.kjv: Thy wickedness may hurt a man as thou art; and thy righteousness may profit the son of man.

35:9.web: “By reason of the multitude of oppressions they cry out. They cry for help by reason of the arm of the mighty.
35:9.kjv: By reason of the multitude of oppressions they make the oppressed to cry: they cry out by reason of the arm of the mighty.

35:10.web: But no one says, ‘Where is God my Maker, who gives songs in the night,
35:10.kjv: But none saith, Where is God my maker, who giveth songs in the night;

35:11.web: who teaches us more than the animals of the earth, and makes us wiser than the birds of the sky?’
35:11.kjv: Who teacheth us more than the beasts of the earth, and maketh us wiser than the fowls of heaven?

35:12.web: There they cry, but no one gives answer, because of the pride of evil men.
35:12.kjv: There they cry, but none giveth answer, because of the pride of evil men.

35:13.web: Surely God will not hear an empty cry, neither will the Almighty regard it.
35:13.kjv: Surely God will not hear vanity, neither will the Almighty regard it.

35:14.web: How much less when you say you don’t see him. The cause is before him, and you wait for him!
35:14.kjv: Although thou sayest thou shalt not see him, yet judgment is before him; therefore trust thou in him.

35:15.web: But now, because he has not visited in his anger, neither does he greatly regard arrogance.
35:15.kjv: But now, because it is not so, he hath visited in his anger; yet he knoweth it not in great extremity:

35:16.web: Therefore Job opens his mouth with empty talk, and he multiplies words without knowledge.”
35:16.kjv: Therefore doth Job open his mouth in vain; he multiplieth words without knowledge.

36:2.web: “Bear with me a little, and I will show you; for I still have something to say on God’s behalf.
36:2.kjv: Suffer me a little, and I will shew thee that I have yet to speak on God’s behalf.

36:3.web: I will get my knowledge from afar, and will ascribe righteousness to my Maker.
36:3.kjv: I will fetch my knowledge from afar, and will ascribe righteousness to my Maker.

36:4.web: For truly my words are not false. One who is perfect in knowledge is with you.
36:4.kjv: For truly my words shall not be false: he that is perfect in knowledge is with thee.

36:5.web: “Behold, God is mighty, and doesn’t despise anyone. He is mighty in strength of understanding.
36:5.kjv: Behold, God is mighty, and despiseth not any: he is mighty in strength and wisdom.

36:6.web: He doesn’t preserve the life of the wicked, but gives to the afflicted their right.
36:6.kjv: He preserveth not the life of the wicked: but giveth right to the poor.

36:7.web: He doesn’t withdraw his eyes from the righteous, but with kings on the throne, he sets them forever, and they are exalted.
36:7.kjv: He withdraweth not his eyes from the righteous: but with kings are they on the throne; yea, he doth establish them for ever, and they are exalted.

36:8.web: If they are bound in fetters, and are taken in the cords of afflictions,
36:8.kjv: And if they be bound in fetters, and be holden in cords of affliction;

36:9.web: then he shows them their work, and their transgressions, that they have behaved themselves proudly.
36:9.kjv: Then he sheweth them their work, and their transgressions that they have exceeded.

36:10.web: He also opens their ears to instruction, and commands that they return from iniquity.
36:10.kjv: He openeth also their ear to discipline, and commandeth that they return from iniquity.

36:11.web: If they listen and serve him, they shall spend their days in prosperity, and their years in pleasures.
36:11.kjv: If they obey and serve him, they shall spend their days in prosperity, and their years in pleasures.

36:12.web: But if they don’t listen, they shall perish by the sword; they shall die without knowledge.
36:12.kjv: But if they obey not, they shall perish by the sword, and they shall die without knowledge.

36:13.web: “But those who are godless in heart lay up anger. They don’t cry for help when he binds them.
36:13.kjv: But the hypocrites in heart heap up wrath: they cry not when he bindeth them.

36:14.web: They die in youth. Their life perishes among the unclean.
36:14.kjv: They die in youth, and their life is among the unclean.

36:15.web: He delivers the afflicted by their affliction, and opens their ear in oppression.
36:15.kjv: He delivereth the poor in his affliction, and openeth their ears in oppression.

36:16.web: Yes, he would have allured you out of distress, into a wide place, where there is no restriction. That which is set on your table would be full of fatness.
36:16.kjv: Even so would he have removed thee out of the strait into a broad place, where there is no straitness; and that which should be set on thy table should be full of fatness.

36:17.web: “But you are full of the judgment of the wicked. Judgment and justice take hold of you.
36:17.kjv: But thou hast fulfilled the judgment of the wicked: judgment and justice take hold on thee.

36:18.web: Don’t let riches entice you to wrath, neither let the great size of a bribe turn you aside.
36:18.kjv: Because there is wrath, beware lest he take thee away with his stroke: then a great ransom cannot deliver thee.

36:19.web: Would your wealth sustain you in distress, or all the might of your strength?
36:19.kjv: Will he esteem thy riches? no, not gold, nor all the forces of strength.

36:20.web: Don’t desire the night, when people are cut off in their place.
36:20.kjv: Desire not the night, when people are cut off in their place.

36:21.web: Take heed, don’t regard iniquity; for you have chosen this rather than affliction.
36:21.kjv: Take heed, regard not iniquity: for this hast thou chosen rather than affliction.

36:22.web: Behold, God is exalted in his power. Who is a teacher like him?
36:22.kjv: Behold, God exalteth by his power: who teacheth like him?

36:23.web: Who has prescribed his way for him? Or who can say, ‘You have committed unrighteousness?’
36:23.kjv: Who hath enjoined him his way? or who can say, Thou hast wrought iniquity?

36:24.web: “Remember that you magnify his work, whereof men have sung.
36:24.kjv: Remember that thou magnify his work, which men behold.

36:25.web: All men have looked on it. Man sees it afar off.
36:25.kjv: Every man may see it; man may behold it afar off.

36:26.web: Behold, God is great, and we don’t know him. The number of his years is unsearchable.
36:26.kjv: Behold, God is great, and we know him not, neither can the number of his years be searched out.

36:27.web: For he draws up the drops of water, which distill in rain from his vapor,
36:27.kjv: For he maketh small the drops of water: they pour down rain according to the vapour thereof:

36:28.web: Which the skies pour down and which drop on man abundantly.
36:28.kjv: Which the clouds do drop and distil upon man abundantly.

36:29.web: Yes, can any understand the spreading of the clouds, and the thunderings of his pavilion?
36:29.kjv: Also can any understand the spreadings of the clouds, or the noise of his tabernacle?

36:30.web: Behold, he spreads his light around him. He covers the bottom of the sea.
36:30.kjv: Behold, he spreadeth his light upon it, and covereth the bottom of the sea.

36:31.web: For by these he judges the people. He gives food in abundance.
36:31.kjv: For by them judgeth he the people; he giveth meat in abundance.

36:32.web: He covers his hands with the lightning, and commands it to strike the mark.
36:32.kjv: With clouds he covereth the light; and commandeth it not to shine by the cloud that cometh betwixt.

36:33.web: Its noise tells about him, and the livestock also concerning the storm that comes up.
36:33.kjv: The noise thereof sheweth concerning it, the cattle also concerning the vapour.

37:1.web: “Yes, at this my heart trembles, and is moved out of its place.
37:1.kjv: At this also my heart trembleth, and is moved out of his place.

37:2.web: Hear, oh, hear the noise of his voice, the sound that goes out of his mouth.
37:2.kjv: Hear attentively the noise of his voice, and the sound that goeth out of his mouth.

37:3.web: He sends it out under the whole sky, and his lightning to the ends of the earth.
37:3.kjv: He directeth it under the whole heaven, and his lightning unto the ends of the earth.

37:4.web: After it a voice roars. He thunders with the voice of his majesty. He doesn’t hold back anything when his voice is heard.
37:4.kjv: After it a voice roareth: he thundereth with the voice of his excellency; and he will not stay them when his voice is heard.

37:5.web: God thunders marvelously with his voice. He does great things, which we can’t comprehend.
37:5.kjv: God thundereth marvellously with his voice; great things doeth he, which we cannot comprehend.

37:6.web: For he says to the snow, ‘Fall on the earth;’ likewise to the shower of rain, and to the showers of his mighty rain.
37:6.kjv: For he saith to the snow, Be thou on the earth; likewise to the small rain, and to the great rain of his strength.

37:7.web: He seals up the hand of every man, that all men whom he has made may know it.
37:7.kjv: He sealeth up the hand of every man; that all men may know his work.

37:8.web: Then the animals take cover, and remain in their dens.
37:8.kjv: Then the beasts go into dens, and remain in their places.

37:9.web: Out of its room comes the storm, and cold out of the north.
37:9.kjv: Out of the south cometh the whirlwind: and cold out of the north.

37:10.web: By the breath of God, ice is given, and the width of the waters is frozen.
37:10.kjv: By the breath of God frost is given: and the breadth of the waters is straitened.

37:11.web: Yes, he loads the thick cloud with moisture. He spreads abroad the cloud of his lightning.
37:11.kjv: Also by watering he wearieth the thick cloud: he scattereth his bright cloud:

37:12.web: It is turned around by his guidance, that they may do whatever he commands them on the surface of the habitable world,
37:12.kjv: And it is turned round about by his counsels: that they may do whatsoever he commandeth them upon the face of the world in the earth.

37:13.web: Whether it is for correction, or for his land, or for loving kindness, that he causes it to come.
37:13.kjv: He causeth it to come, whether for correction, or for his land, or for mercy.

37:14.web: “Listen to this, Job. Stand still, and consider the wondrous works of God.
37:14.kjv: Hearken unto this, O Job: stand still, and consider the wondrous works of God.

37:15.web: Do you know how God controls them, and causes the lightning of his cloud to shine?
37:15.kjv: Dost thou know when God disposed them, and caused the light of his cloud to shine?

37:16.web: Do you know the workings of the clouds, the wondrous works of him who is perfect in knowledge?
37:16.kjv: Dost thou know the balancings of the clouds, the wondrous works of him which is perfect in knowledge?

37:17.web: You whose clothing is warm, when the earth is still by reason of the south wind?
37:17.kjv: How thy garments are warm, when he quieteth the earth by the south wind?

37:18.web: Can you, with him, spread out the sky, which is strong as a cast metal mirror?
37:18.kjv: Hast thou with him spread out the sky, which is strong, and as a molten looking glass?

37:19.web: Teach us what we shall tell him, for we can’t make our case by reason of darkness.
37:19.kjv: Teach us what we shall say unto him; for we cannot order our speech by reason of darkness.

37:20.web: Will it be told him that I would speak? Or should a man wish that he were swallowed up?
37:20.kjv: Shall it be told him that I speak? if a man speak, surely he shall be swallowed up.

37:21.web: Now men don’t see the light which is bright in the skies, but the wind passes, and clears them.
37:21.kjv: And now men see not the bright light which is in the clouds: but the wind passeth, and cleanseth them.

37:22.web: Out of the north comes golden splendor. With God is awesome majesty.
37:22.kjv: Fair weather cometh out of the north: with God is terrible majesty.

37:23.web: We can’t reach the Almighty. He is exalted in power. In justice and great righteousness, he will not oppress.
37:23.kjv: Touching the Almighty, we cannot find him out: he is excellent in power, and in judgment, and in plenty of justice: he will not afflict.

37:24.web: Therefore men revere him. He doesn’t regard any who are wise of heart.”
37:24.kjv: Men do therefore fear him: he respecteth not any that are wise of heart.

38:1.web: Then Yahweh answered Job out of the whirlwind,
38:1.kjv: Then the LORD answered Job out of the whirlwind, and said,

38:2.web: “Who is this who darkens counsel by words without knowledge?
38:2.kjv: Who is this that darkeneth counsel by words without knowledge?

38:3.web: Brace yourself like a man, for I will question you, then you answer me!
38:3.kjv: Gird up now thy loins like a man; for I will demand of thee, and answer thou me.

38:4.web: “Where were you when I laid the foundations of the earth? Declare, if you have understanding.
38:4.kjv: Where wast thou when I laid the foundations of the earth? declare, if thou hast understanding.

38:5.web: Who determined its measures, if you know? Or who stretched the line on it?
38:5.kjv: Who hath laid the measures thereof, if thou knowest? or who hath stretched the line upon it?

38:6.web: Whereupon were its foundations fastened? Or who laid its cornerstone,
38:6.kjv: Whereupon are the foundations thereof fastened? or who laid the corner stone thereof;

38:7.web: when the morning stars sang together, and all the sons of God shouted for joy?
38:7.kjv: When the morning stars sang together, and all the sons of God shouted for joy?

38:8.web: “Or who shut up the sea with doors, when it broke out of the womb,
38:8.kjv: Or who shut up the sea with doors, when it brake forth, as if it had issued out of the womb?

38:9.web: when I made clouds its garment, and wrapped it in thick darkness,
38:9.kjv: When I made the cloud the garment thereof, and thick darkness a swaddlingband for it,

38:10.web: marked out for it my bound, set bars and doors,
38:10.kjv: And brake up for it my decreed place, and set bars and doors,

38:11.web: and said, ‘Here you may come, but no further. Here your proud waves shall be stayed?’
38:11.kjv: And said, Hitherto shalt thou come, but no further: and here shall thy proud waves be stayed?

38:12.web: “Have you commanded the morning in your days, and caused the dawn to know its place;
38:12.kjv: Hast thou commanded the morning since thy days; and caused the dayspring to know his place;

38:13.web: that it might take hold of the ends of the earth, and shake the wicked out of it?
38:13.kjv: That it might take hold of the ends of the earth, that the wicked might be shaken out of it?

38:14.web: It is changed as clay under the seal, and presented as a garment.
38:14.kjv: It is turned as clay to the seal; and they stand as a garment.

38:15.web: From the wicked, their light is withheld. The high arm is broken.
38:15.kjv: And from the wicked their light is withholden, and the high arm shall be broken.

38:16.web: “Have you entered into the springs of the sea? Or have you walked in the recesses of the deep?
38:16.kjv: Hast thou entered into the springs of the sea? or hast thou walked in the search of the depth?

38:17.web: Have the gates of death been revealed to you? Or have you seen the gates of the shadow of death?
38:17.kjv: Have the gates of death been opened unto thee? or hast thou seen the doors of the shadow of death?

38:18.web: Have you comprehended the earth in its width? Declare, if you know it all.
38:18.kjv: Hast thou perceived the breadth of the earth? declare if thou knowest it all.

38:19.web: “What is the way to the dwelling of light? As for darkness, where is its place,
38:19.kjv: Where is the way where light dwelleth? and as for darkness, where is the place thereof,

38:20.web: that you should take it to its bound, that you should discern the paths to its house?
38:20.kjv: That thou shouldest take it to the bound thereof, and that thou shouldest know the paths to the house thereof?

38:21.web: Surely you know, for you were born then, and the number of your days is great!
38:21.kjv: Knowest thou it, because thou wast then born? or because the number of thy days is great?

38:22.web: Have you entered the treasuries of the snow, or have you seen the treasures of the hail,
38:22.kjv: Hast thou entered into the treasures of the snow? or hast thou seen the treasures of the hail,

38:23.web: which I have reserved against the time of trouble, against the day of battle and war?
38:23.kjv: Which I have reserved against the time of trouble, against the day of battle and war?

38:24.web: By what way is the lightning distributed, or the east wind scattered on the earth?
38:24.kjv: By what way is the light parted, which scattereth the east wind upon the earth?

38:25.web: Who has cut a channel for the flood water, or the path for the thunderstorm;
38:25.kjv: Who hath divided a watercourse for the overflowing of waters, or a way for the lightning of thunder;

38:26.web: To cause it to rain on a land where no man is; on the wilderness, in which there is no man;
38:26.kjv: To cause it to rain on the earth, where no man is; on the wilderness, wherein there is no man;

38:27.web: to satisfy the waste and desolate ground, to cause the tender grass to grow?
38:27.kjv: To satisfy the desolate and waste ground; and to cause the bud of the tender herb to spring forth?

38:28.web: Does the rain have a father? Or who fathers the drops of dew?
38:28.kjv: Hath the rain a father? or who hath begotten the drops of dew?

38:29.web: Out of whose womb came the ice? The gray frost of the sky, who has given birth to it?
38:29.kjv: Out of whose womb came the ice? and the hoary frost of heaven, who hath gendered it?

38:30.web: The waters become hard like stone, when the surface of the deep is frozen.
38:30.kjv: The waters are hid as with a stone, and the face of the deep is frozen.

38:31.web: “Can you bind the cluster of the Pleiades, or loosen the cords of Orion?
38:31.kjv: Canst thou bind the sweet influences of Pleiades, or loose the bands of Orion?

38:32.web: Can you lead the constellations out in their season? Or can you guide the Bear with her cubs?
38:32.kjv: Canst thou bring forth Mazzaroth in his season? or canst thou guide Arcturus with his sons?

38:33.web: Do you know the laws of the heavens? Can you establish its dominion over the earth?
38:33.kjv: Knowest thou the ordinances of heaven? canst thou set the dominion thereof in the earth?

38:34.web: “Can you lift up your voice to the clouds, That abundance of waters may cover you?
38:34.kjv: Canst thou lift up thy voice to the clouds, that abundance of waters may cover thee?

38:35.web: Can you send out lightnings, that they may go? Do they report to you, ‘Here we are?’
38:35.kjv: Canst thou send lightnings, that they may go, and say unto thee, Here we are?

38:36.web: Who has put wisdom in the inward parts? Or who has given understanding to the mind?
38:36.kjv: Who hath put wisdom in the inward parts? or who hath given understanding to the heart?

38:37.web: Who can count the clouds by wisdom? Or who can pour out the bottles of the sky,
38:37.kjv: Who can number the clouds in wisdom? or who can stay the bottles of heaven,

38:38.web: when the dust runs into a mass, and the clods of earth stick together?
38:38.kjv: When the dust groweth into hardness, and the clods cleave fast together?

38:39.web: “Can you hunt the prey for the lioness, or satisfy the appetite of the young lions,
38:39.kjv: Wilt thou hunt the prey for the lion? or fill the appetite of the young lions,

38:40.web: when they crouch in their dens, and lie in wait in the thicket?
38:40.kjv: When they couch in their dens, and abide in the covert to lie in wait?

38:41.web: Who provides for the raven his prey, when his young ones cry to God, and wander for lack of food?
38:41.kjv: Who provideth for the raven his food? when his young ones cry unto God, they wander for lack of meat.

39:1.web: “Do you know the time when the mountain goats give birth? Do you watch when the doe bears fawns?
39:1.kjv: Knowest thou the time when the wild goats of the rock bring forth? or canst thou mark when the hinds do calve?

39:2.web: Can you count the months that they fulfill? Or do you know the time when they give birth?
39:2.kjv: Canst thou number the months that they fulfil? or knowest thou the time when they bring forth?

39:3.web: They bow themselves, they bear their young. They end their labor pains.
39:3.kjv: They bow themselves, they bring forth their young ones, they cast out their sorrows.

39:4.web: Their young ones become strong. They grow up in the open field. They go out, and don’t return again.
39:4.kjv: Their young ones are in good liking, they grow up with corn; they go forth, and return not unto them.

39:5.web: “Who has set the wild donkey free? Or who has loosened the bonds of the swift donkey,
39:5.kjv: Who hath sent out the wild ass free? or who hath loosed the bands of the wild ass?

39:6.web: Whose home I have made the wilderness, and the salt land his dwelling place?
39:6.kjv: Whose house I have made the wilderness, and the barren land his dwellings.

39:7.web: He scorns the tumult of the city, neither does he hear the shouting of the driver.
39:7.kjv: He scorneth the multitude of the city, neither regardeth he the crying of the driver.

39:8.web: The range of the mountains is his pasture, He searches after every green thing.
39:8.kjv: The range of the mountains is his pasture, and he searcheth after every green thing.

39:9.web: “Will the wild ox be content to serve you? Or will he stay by your feeding trough?
39:9.kjv: Will the unicorn be willing to serve thee, or abide by thy crib?

39:10.web: Can you hold the wild ox in the furrow with his harness? Or will he till the valleys after you?
39:10.kjv: Canst thou bind the unicorn with his band in the furrow? or will he harrow the valleys after thee?

39:11.web: Will you trust him, because his strength is great? Or will you leave to him your labor?
39:11.kjv: Wilt thou trust him, because his strength is great? or wilt thou leave thy labour to him?

39:12.web: Will you confide in him, that he will bring home your seed, and gather the grain of your threshing floor?
39:12.kjv: Wilt thou believe him, that he will bring home thy seed, and gather it into thy barn?

39:13.web: “The wings of the ostrich wave proudly; but are they the feathers and plumage of love?
39:13.kjv: Gavest thou the goodly wings unto the peacocks? or wings and feathers unto the ostrich?

39:14.web: For she leaves her eggs on the earth, warms them in the dust,
39:14.kjv: Which leaveth her eggs in the earth, and warmeth them in dust,

39:15.web: and forgets that the foot may crush them, or that the wild animal may trample them.
39:15.kjv: And forgetteth that the foot may crush them, or that the wild beast may break them.

39:16.web: She deals harshly with her young ones, as if they were not hers. Though her labor is in vain, she is without fear,
39:16.kjv: She is hardened against her young ones, as though they were not hers: her labour is in vain without fear;

39:17.web: because God has deprived her of wisdom, neither has he imparted to her understanding.
39:17.kjv: Because God hath deprived her of wisdom, neither hath he imparted to her understanding.

39:18.web: When she lifts up herself on high, she scorns the horse and his rider.
39:18.kjv: What time she lifteth up herself on high, she scorneth the horse and his rider.

39:19.web: “Have you given the horse might? Have you clothed his neck with a quivering mane?
39:19.kjv: Hath thou given the horse strength? hast thou clothed his neck with thunder?

39:20.web: Have you made him to leap as a locust? The glory of his snorting is awesome.
39:20.kjv: Canst thou make him afraid as a grasshopper? the glory of his nostrils is terrible.

39:21.web: He paws in the valley, and rejoices in his strength. He goes out to meet the armed men.
39:21.kjv: He paweth in the valley, and rejoiceth in his strength: he goeth on to meet the armed men.

39:22.web: He mocks at fear, and is not dismayed, neither does he turn back from the sword.
39:22.kjv: He mocketh at fear, and is not affrighted; neither turneth he back from the sword.

39:23.web: The quiver rattles against him, the flashing spear and the javelin.
39:23.kjv: The quiver rattleth against him, the glittering spear and the shield.

39:24.web: He eats up the ground with fierceness and rage, neither does he stand still at the sound of the trumpet.
39:24.kjv: He swalloweth the ground with fierceness and rage: neither believeth he that it is the sound of the trumpet.

39:25.web: As often as the trumpet sounds he snorts, ‘Aha!’ He smells the battle afar off, the thunder of the captains, and the shouting.
39:25.kjv: He saith among the trumpets, Ha, ha; and he smelleth the battle afar off, the thunder of the captains, and the shouting.

39:26.web: “Is it by your wisdom that the hawk soars, and stretches her wings toward the south?
39:26.kjv: Doth the hawk fly by thy wisdom, and stretch her wings toward the south?

39:27.web: Is it at your command that the eagle mounts up, and makes his nest on high?
39:27.kjv: Doth the eagle mount up at thy command, and make her nest on high?

39:28.web: On the cliff he dwells, and makes his home, on the point of the cliff, and the stronghold.
39:28.kjv: She dwelleth and abideth on the rock, upon the crag of the rock, and the strong place.

39:29.web: From there he spies out the prey. His eyes see it afar off.
39:29.kjv: From thence she seeketh the prey, and her eyes behold afar off.

39:30.web: His young ones also suck up blood. Where the slain are, there he is.”
39:30.kjv: Her young ones also suck up blood: and where the slain are, there is she.

40:1.kjv: Moreover the LORD answered Job, and said,

40:2.web: “Shall he who argues contend with the Almighty? He who argues with God, let him answer it.”
40:2.kjv: Shall he that contendeth with the Almighty instruct him? he that reproveth God, let him answer it.

40:3.kjv: Then Job answered the LORD, and said,

40:4.web: “Behold, I am of small account. What shall I answer you? I lay my hand on my mouth.
40:4.kjv: Behold, I am vile; what shall I answer thee? I will lay mine hand upon my mouth.

40:5.web: I have spoken once, and I will not answer; Yes, twice, but I will proceed no further.”
40:5.kjv: Once have I spoken; but I will not answer: yea, twice; but I will proceed no further.

40:6.web: Then Yahweh answered Job out of the whirlwind,
40:6.kjv: Then answered the LORD unto Job out of the whirlwind, and said,

40:7.web: “Now brace yourself like a man. I will question you, and you will answer me.
40:7.kjv: Gird up thy loins now like a man: I will demand of thee, and declare thou unto me.

40:8.web: Will you even annul my judgment? Will you condemn me, that you may be justified?
40:8.kjv: Wilt thou also disannul my judgment? wilt thou condemn me, that thou mayest be righteous?

40:9.web: Or do you have an arm like God? Can you thunder with a voice like him?
40:9.kjv: Hast thou an arm like God? or canst thou thunder with a voice like him?

40:10.web: “Now deck yourself with excellency and dignity. Array yourself with honor and majesty.
40:10.kjv: Deck thyself now with majesty and excellency; and array thyself with glory and beauty.

40:11.web: Pour out the fury of your anger. Look at everyone who is proud, and bring him low.
40:11.kjv: Cast abroad the rage of thy wrath: and behold every one that is proud, and abase him.

40:12.web: Look at everyone who is proud, and humble him. Crush the wicked in their place.
40:12.kjv: Look on every one that is proud, and bring him low; and tread down the wicked in their place.

40:13.web: Hide them in the dust together. Bind their faces in the hidden place.
40:13.kjv: Hide them in the dust together; and bind their faces in secret.

40:14.web: Then I will also admit to you that your own right hand can save you.
40:14.kjv: Then will I also confess unto thee that thine own right hand can save thee.

40:15.web: “See now, behemoth, which I made as well as you. He eats grass as an ox.
40:15.kjv: Behold now behemoth, which I made with thee; he eateth grass as an ox.

40:16.web: Look now, his strength is in his thighs. His force is in the muscles of his belly.
40:16.kjv: Lo now, his strength is in his loins, and his force is in the navel of his belly.

40:17.web: He moves his tail like a cedar. The sinews of his thighs are knit together.
40:17.kjv: He moveth his tail like a cedar: the sinews of his stones are wrapped together.

40:18.web: His bones are like tubes of brass. His limbs are like bars of iron.
40:18.kjv: His bones are as strong pieces of brass; his bones are like bars of iron.

40:19.web: He is the chief of the ways of God. He who made him gives him his sword.
40:19.kjv: He is the chief of the ways of God: he that made him can make his sword to approach unto him.

40:20.web: Surely the mountains produce food for him, where all the animals of the field play.
40:20.kjv: Surely the mountains bring him forth food, where all the beasts of the field play.

40:21.web: He lies under the lotus trees, in the covert of the reed, and the marsh.
40:21.kjv: He lieth under the shady trees, in the covert of the reed, and fens.

40:22.web: The lotuses cover him with their shade. The willows of the brook surround him.
40:22.kjv: The shady trees cover him with their shadow; the willows of the brook compass him about.

40:23.web: Behold, if a river overflows, he doesn’t tremble. He is confident, though the Jordan swells even to his mouth.
40:23.kjv: Behold, he drinketh up a river, and hasteth not: he trusteth that he can draw up Jordan into his mouth.

40:24.web: Shall any take him when he is on the watch, or pierce through his nose with a snare?
40:24.kjv: He taketh it with his eyes: his nose pierceth through snares.

41:1.web: “Can you draw out Leviathan with a fish hook, or press down his tongue with a cord?
41:1.kjv: Canst thou draw out leviathan with an hook? or his tongue with a cord which thou lettest down?

41:2.web: Can you put a rope into his nose, or pierce his jaw through with a hook?
41:2.kjv: Canst thou put an hook into his nose? or bore his jaw through with a thorn?

41:3.web: Will he make many petitions to you, or will he speak soft words to you?
41:3.kjv: Will he make many supplications unto thee? will he speak soft words unto thee?

41:4.web: Will he make a covenant with you, that you should take him for a servant forever?
41:4.kjv: Will he make a covenant with thee? wilt thou take him for a servant for ever?

bsb: or put him on a leash
41:5.web: Will you play with him as with a bird? Or will you bind him for your girls?
41:5.kjv: Wilt thou play with him as with a bird? or wilt thou bind him for thy maidens?

41:6.web: Will traders barter for him? Will they part him among the merchants?
41:6.kjv: Shall the companions make a banquet of him? shall they part him among the merchants?

41:7.web: Can you fill his skin with barbed irons, or his head with fish spears?
41:7.kjv: Canst thou fill his skin with barbed irons? or his head with fish spears?

41:8.web: Lay your hand on him. Remember the battle, and do so no more.
41:8.kjv: Lay thine hand upon him, remember the battle, do no more.

41:9.web: Behold, the hope of him is in vain. Won’t one be cast down even at the sight of him?
41:9.kjv: Behold, the hope of him is in vain: shall not one be cast down even at the sight of him?

41:10.web: None is so fierce that he dare stir him up. Who then is he who can stand before me?
41:10.kjv: None is so fierce that dare stir him up: who then is able to stand before me?

41:11.web: Who has first given to me, that I should repay him? Everything under the heavens is mine.
41:11.kjv: Who hath prevented me, that I should repay him? whatsoever is under the whole heaven is mine.

41:12.web: “I will not keep silence concerning his limbs, nor his mighty strength, nor his goodly frame.
41:12.kjv: I will not conceal his parts, nor his power, nor his comely proportion.

41:13.web: Who can strip off his outer garment? Who shall come within his jaws?
41:13.kjv: Who can discover the face of his garment? or who can come to him with his double bridle?

41:14.web: Who can open the doors of his face? Around his teeth is terror.
41:14.kjv: Who can open the doors of his face? his teeth are terrible round about.

41:15.web: Strong scales are his pride, shut up together with a close seal.
41:15.kjv: His scales are his pride, shut up together as with a close seal.

41:16.web: One is so near to another, that no air can come between them.
41:16.kjv: One is so near to another, that no air can come between them.

41:17.web: They are joined to one another. They stick together, so that they can’t be pulled apart.
41:17.kjv: They are joined one to another, they stick together, that they cannot be sundered.

41:18.web: His sneezing flashes out light. His eyes are like the eyelids of the morning.
41:18.kjv: By his neesings a light doth shine, and his eyes are like the eyelids of the morning.

41:19.web: Out of his mouth go burning torches. Sparks of fire leap out.
41:19.kjv: Out of his mouth go burning lamps, and sparks of fire leap out.

41:20.web: Out of his nostrils a smoke goes, as of a boiling pot over a fire of reeds.
41:20.kjv: Out of his nostrils goeth smoke, as out of a seething pot or caldron.

41:21.web: His breath kindles coals. A flame goes out of his mouth.
41:21.kjv: His breath kindleth coals, and a flame goeth out of his mouth.

41:22.web: There is strength in his neck. Terror dances before him.
41:22.kjv: In his neck remaineth strength, and sorrow is turned into joy before him.

41:23.web: The flakes of his flesh are joined together. They are firm on him. They can’t be moved.
41:23.kjv: The flakes of his flesh are joined together: they are firm in themselves; they cannot be moved.

41:24.web: His heart is as firm as a stone, yes, firm as the lower millstone.
41:24.kjv: His heart is as firm as a stone; yea, as hard as a piece of the nether millstone.

41:25.web: When he raises himself up, the mighty are afraid. They retreat before his thrashing.
41:25.kjv: When he raiseth up himself, the mighty are afraid: by reason of breakings they purify themselves.

41:26.web: If one attacks him with the sword, it can’t prevail; nor the spear, the dart, nor the pointed shaft.
41:26.kjv: The sword of him that layeth at him cannot hold: the spear, the dart, nor the habergeon.

41:27.web: He counts iron as straw; and brass as rotten wood.
41:27.kjv: He esteemeth iron as straw, and brass as rotten wood.

41:28.web: The arrow can’t make him flee. Sling stones are like chaff to him.
41:28.kjv: The arrow cannot make him flee: slingstones are turned with him into stubble.

41:29.web: Clubs are counted as stubble. He laughs at the rushing of the javelin.
41:29.kjv: Darts are counted as stubble: he laugheth at the shaking of a spear.

41:30.web: His undersides are like sharp potsherds, leaving a trail in the mud like a threshing sledge.
41:30.kjv: Sharp stones are under him: he spreadeth sharp pointed things upon the mire.

41:31.web: He makes the deep to boil like a pot. He makes the sea like a pot of ointment.
41:31.kjv: He maketh the deep to boil like a pot: he maketh the sea like a pot of ointment.

41:32.web: He makes a path shine after him. One would think the deep had white hair.
41:32.kjv: He maketh a path to shine after him; one would think the deep to be hoary.

41:33.web: On earth there is not his equal, that is made without fear.
41:33.kjv: Upon earth there is not his like, who is made without fear.

41:34.web: He sees everything that is high. He is king over all the sons of pride.”
41:34.kjv: He beholdeth all high things: he is a king over all the children of pride.

42:1.kjv: Then Job answered the LORD, and said,

42:2.web: “I know that you can do all things, and that no purpose of yours can be restrained.
42:2.kjv: I know that thou canst do every thing, and that no thought can be withholden from thee.

42:3.web: You asked, ‘Who is this who hides counsel without knowledge?’ therefore I have uttered that which I did not understand, things too wonderful for me, which I didn’t know.
42:3.kjv: Who is he that hideth counsel without knowledge? therefore have I uttered that I understood not; things too wonderful for me, which I knew not.

42:4.web: You said, ‘Listen, now, and I will speak; I will question you, and you will answer me.’
42:4.kjv: Hear, I beseech thee, and I will speak: I will demand of thee, and declare thou unto me.

42:5.web: I had heard of you by the hearing of the ear, but now my eye sees you.
42:5.kjv: I have heard of thee by the hearing of the ear: but now mine eye seeth thee.

42:6.web: Therefore I abhor myself, and repent in dust and ashes.”
42:6.kjv: Wherefore I abhor myself, and repent in dust and ashes.

42:7.web: It was so, that after Yahweh had spoken these words to Job, Yahweh said to Eliphaz the Temanite, “My wrath is kindled against you, and against your two friends; for you have not spoken of me the thing that is right, as my servant Job has.
42:7.kjv: And it was so, that after the LORD had spoken these words unto Job, the LORD said to Eliphaz the Temanite, My wrath is kindled against thee, and against thy two friends: for ye have not spoken of me the thing that is right, as my servant Job hath.

42:8.web: Now therefore, take to yourselves seven bulls and seven rams, and go to my servant Job, and offer up for yourselves a burnt offering; and my servant Job shall pray for you, for I will accept him, that I not deal with you according to your folly. For you have not spoken of me the thing that is right, as my servant Job has.”
42:8.kjv: Therefore take unto you now seven bullocks and seven rams, and go to my servant Job, and offer up for yourselves a burnt offering; and my servant Job shall pray for you: for him will I accept: lest I deal with you after your folly, in that ye have not spoken of me the thing which is right, like my servant Job.

42:9.web: So Eliphaz the Temanite and Bildad the Shuhite and Zophar the Naamathite went, and did what Yahweh commanded them, and Yahweh accepted Job.
42:9.kjv: So Eliphaz the Temanite and Bildad the Shuhite and Zophar the Naamathite went, and did according as the LORD commanded them: the LORD also accepted Job.

42:10.web: Yahweh turned the captivity of Job, when he prayed for his friends. Yahweh gave Job twice as much as he had before.
42:10.kjv: And the LORD turned the captivity of Job, when he prayed for his friends: also the LORD gave Job twice as much as he had before.

42:11.web: Then came there to him all his brothers, and all his sisters, and all those who had been of his acquaintance before, and ate bread with him in his house. They comforted him, and consoled him concerning all the evil that Yahweh had brought on him. Everyone also gave him a piece of money, and everyone a ring of gold.
42:11.kjv: Then came there unto him all his brethren, and all his sisters, and all they that had been of his acquaintance before, and did eat bread with him in his house: and they bemoaned him, and comforted him over all the evil that the LORD had brought upon him: every man also gave him a piece of money, and every one an earring of gold.

42:12.web: So Yahweh blessed the latter end of Job more than his beginning. He had fourteen thousand sheep, six thousand camels, one thousand yoke of oxen, and a thousand female donkeys.
42:12.kjv: So the LORD blessed the latter end of Job more than his beginning: for he had fourteen thousand sheep, and six thousand camels, and a thousand yoke of oxen, and a thousand she asses.

42:13.web: He had also seven sons and three daughters.
42:13.kjv: He had also seven sons and three daughters.

42:14.web: He called the name of the first, Jemimah; and the name of the second, Keziah; and the name of the third, Keren Happuch.
42:14.kjv: And he called the name of the first, Jemima; and the name of the second, Kezia; and the name of the third, Keren-happuch.

42:15.web: In all the land were no women found so beautiful as the daughters of Job. Their father gave them an inheritance among their brothers.
42:15.kjv: And in all the land were no women found so fair as the daughters of Job: and their father gave them inheritance among their brethren.

42:16.web: After this Job lived one hundred forty years, and saw his sons, and his sons’ sons, to four generations.
42:16.kjv: After this lived Job an hundred and forty years, and saw his sons, and his sons’ sons, even four generations.

42:17.web: So Job died, being old and full of days.
42:17.kjv: So Job died, being old and full of days.
